cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A molecule is recognised by an antibody but does not by itself trigger an immune response. Which term fits best? Antigen that is not an immunogen All immunogens are antigens, but not all antigens are immunogens. Haptens are the classic example that need a carrier. Lecture 02 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: What is an epitope? The small part of an antigen bound by one antibody An epitope (antigenic determinant) is the small part of an antigen bound by one antibody. Lecture 02 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which test is an example of serology? Measuring HBsAg or anti-HIV in serum Serology is antigen–antibody testing of serum, with HBsAg and anti-HIV as the examples on the slide. Lecture 02 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which cells produce antibodies? Plasma cells derived from B lymphocytes Antibodies are glycoproteins secreted by plasma cells, which derive from B lymphocytes. Lecture 02 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which line of defence consists of phagocytic cells? Line 2 Line 1 = barriers, line 2 = phagocytes (both innate), line 3 = humoral, line 4 = cell-mediated (adaptive). Lecture 02 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Encapsulated bacteria that evade phagocytosis are best handled by which line of defence? Line 3 – antibodies that enhance phagocytosis The slide says antibodies (humoral immunity, line 3) help overcome the capsule by enhancing phagocytosis. Lecture 02 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A person gets a splinter. A second splinter weeks later triggers exactly the same response. This illustrates: Innate immunity, with no memory The splinter story shows the innate response is the same each time, starting within minutes with inflammation within hours. Lecture 02 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Pattern-recognition receptors such as TLRs recognise: PAMPs and DAMPs Innate cells sense PAMPs on microbes and DAMPs from damaged cells through PRRs like TLRs. Lecture 02 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which statement about “trained immunity” fits the slide? Innate cells can be reprogrammed despite no classic memory The slide notes that innate immunity is generally non-memory, although trained immunity shows innate cells can be reprogrammed. Lecture 02 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which feature belongs to adaptive, not innate, immunity? Rearranged BCR/TCR giving about 10⁷–10⁹ clones Adaptive receptors are rearranged by V(D)J recombination. Innate receptors are germline-encoded. Lecture 02 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: MHC class II molecules present peptide to which cell? CD4⁺ T cells MHC class I → CD8⁺ T cells; MHC class II → CD4⁺ T cells. Lecture 02 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which is signal 2 for a naïve T cell? Co-stimulation (B7–CD28) Signal 1 = TCR–peptide–MHC, signal 2 = co-stimulation (B7–CD28), signal 3 = cytokines. Lecture 02 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which antibody isotype is first to appear in a primary response? IgM IgM appears first; IgG dominates later and in the secondary response. Lecture 02 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which isotype crosses the placenta? IgG IgG is the main antibody and is the one that crosses the placenta. Lecture 02 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which Th subset activates macrophages? Th1 Th1 activate macrophages; Th2 eosinophils; Th17 neutrophils; Tfh help B cells make high-affinity antibodies. Lecture 02 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which T-cell subset helps B cells make high-affinity antibodies? Tfh Tfh (follicular helper) cells help B cells make high-affinity antibodies. Lecture 02 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A child receives rabies immunoglobulin after a bite. This is: Artificial passive immunity Ready-made antibodies given medically are artificial passive immunity. Passive protection is immediate but short-lived, without memory. Lecture 02 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which example is natural passive immunity? IgA in breast milk Maternal IgG across the placenta and IgA in milk are natural passive immunity. Lecture 02 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which of the following is true of the secondary response compared with the primary response? Lag of 1–3 days, mainly IgG, 10–100× greater Memory lymphocytes give a lag of 1–3 days with mainly higher-affinity IgG, 10–100× greater and longer-lasting. Lecture 02 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Mutation of the RAG genes would most directly lead to: SCID RAG genes drive V(D)J recombination. RAG defects → SCID. Lecture 02 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A defect in FOXP3 causes which condition? IPEX FOXP3 defect (regulatory T cells) → IPEX; AIRE defect → APS-1. Lecture 02 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which mechanism is part of PERIPHERAL tolerance? Anergy, deletion and suppression by Tregs Strongly self-reactive cells are deleted centrally (thymus for T, bone marrow for B); peripheral tolerance uses anergy, deletion and Treg suppression. Lecture 02 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which failure of immunity is defined as “too much response to harmless antigens”? Hypersensitivity Hypersensitivity = overreaction to harmless antigens; autoimmunity = loss of self-tolerance; immunodeficiency = absent/weak response; immunoproliferative = malignant immune cells. Lecture 02 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which agent restores neutrophil numbers after chemotherapy? G-CSF (filgrastim) G-CSF stimulates the bone marrow to produce neutrophils. Lecture 03 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Where do T cells mature? Thymus T cells mature in the thymus; NK and B cells mature in the bone marrow. Lecture 03 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which of the following is a component of innate immunity? Complement proteins Complement, acute-phase proteins, cytokines and antimicrobial peptides are innate soluble molecules. Lecture 03 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: What is the main role of lysozyme? Digest peptidoglycan in bacterial cell walls Lysozyme in tears and saliva digests peptidoglycan. Lecture 03 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Defensins and cathelicidin (LL-37) work by: Disrupting microbial membranes They are antimicrobial peptides that disrupt microbial membranes. Lecture 03 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which is a defence of the stomach against ingested bacteria? Gastric acid at pH 1–3 Gastric acid (pH 1–3), bile, peristalsis and Paneth-cell defensins protect the gut. Lecture 03 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: The mucociliary escalator is impaired in: Cystic fibrosis and smoking The slide lists cystic fibrosis and smoking as impairing mucociliary clearance. Lecture 03 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which organism pair is linked to antibiotic disturbance of normal flora? Candida overgrowth and C. difficile colitis Antibiotics disturb the microbiota, allowing Candida overgrowth and C. difficile colitis. Lecture 03 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Microbiota therapies approved to prevent recurrent infection target which organism? C. difficile Rebyota and Vowst are named for preventing recurrent C. difficile. Lecture 03 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: In the burn case, which defence failed first? The skin barrier The skin barrier was lost, with burn-induced immune suppression. Lecture 03 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which organism grew from the burn wound and blood cultures? Pseudomonas aeruginosa The case describes Pseudomonas aeruginosa, an opportunist that forms biofilms and is often drug-resistant. Lecture 03 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: What is the priority management step in the burn sepsis case? Cultures and antipseudomonal antibiotics within 1 hour, fluids and wound excision The slide lists cultures, antipseudomonal antibiotics within 1 h, fluids and wound excision. Lecture 03 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which TLR recognises LPS? TLR4 TLR4 = LPS; TLR2 = lipoproteins; TLR5 = flagellin. Lecture 03 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Flagellin is sensed by: TLR5 TLR5 detects bacterial flagellin. Lecture 03 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which receptor senses viral RNA in the cytosol? RIG-I RIG-I detects viral RNA; cGAS–STING senses DNA. Lecture 03 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which pathway senses cytosolic DNA? cGAS–STING cGAS–STING is the DNA-sensing pathway on the slide. Lecture 03 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Caspase-1 activation by NLRP3 leads to production of: Active IL-1β NLR activation → caspase-1 → active IL-1β; triggered by microbes and urate crystals (gout). Lecture 03 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A patient has recurrent fevers and inflammation due to an NLRP3 gain-of-function mutation. Which treatment fits? IL-1 blockade NLRP3 mutations cause CAPS, treated with IL-1 blockade. Lecture 03 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: NF-κB activation mainly results in: Inflammatory cytokines NF-κB → inflammatory cytokines; IRFs → type I interferons. Lecture 03 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Heplisav-B contains an adjuvant that stimulates which receptor? TLR9 (CpG) The TLR9 agonist CpG is the vaccine adjuvant in Heplisav-B. Lecture 03 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which of the following is a chemoattractant for phagocytes? C5a Phagocytes move up gradients of C5a, CXCL8, bacterial fMLP peptides and LTB4. C3b and IgG are opsonins. Lecture 04 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which molecules are opsonins named on the slide? C3b and IgG Opsonins that enhance attachment include C3b and IgG (also CRP and MBL). Lecture 04 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: What is a phagosome? A vesicle containing the engulfed microbe Pseudopods surround the microbe, forming a phagosome that then fuses with lysosomes. Lecture 04 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A patient without a spleen is most at risk from: Encapsulated bacteria such as S. pneumoniae The spleen clears opsonised encapsulated bacteria. Asplenic patients need vaccines against N. meningitidis, S. pneumoniae and H. influenzae. Lecture 04 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which of the following is an encapsulated bacterium? Haemophilus influenzae type B The listed examples include S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae type B, N. meningitidis, E. coli, Salmonella, Klebsiella and group B Strep. Lecture 04 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which adhesion molecules mediate rolling of leukocytes on activated endothelium? E- and P-selectins Selectins mediate rolling. LFA-1 and Mac-1 bind ICAM-1 for firm adhesion after chemokines switch integrins to high affinity. Lecture 04 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which integrins bind ICAM-1? LFA-1 and Mac-1 LFA-1 and Mac-1 bind ICAM-1 for firm adhesion. Lecture 04 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: After tissue injury, which cells arrive first and when? Neutrophils at 6–24 h Neutrophils arrive first (6–24 h), followed by monocytes (24–48 h). Lecture 04 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A newborn has delayed umbilical cord separation, infections without pus and high neutrophil counts. Which defect fits? LAD-I (CD18 defect) LAD-I causes delayed cord separation, infections without pus and neutrophilia. Lecture 04 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Natalizumab, used for multiple sclerosis, blocks: α4 integrin Natalizumab is anti-α4 integrin and blocks leukocyte entry into tissue. Lecture 04 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which enzyme converts H₂O₂ to hypochlorous acid in neutrophils? Myeloperoxidase NADPH oxidase makes superoxide, which gives H₂O₂; myeloperoxidase turns this into hypochlorous acid (bleach). Lecture 04 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which cell source of nitric oxide is described on the slide? Activated macrophages via iNOS Inducible NO synthase in activated macrophages produces NO. Lecture 04 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which feature describes neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs)? DNA webs with granule proteins that trap microbes NETs are DNA webs studded with granule proteins; they may also drive thrombosis and autoimmunity. Lecture 04 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A child has recurrent S. aureus and Aspergillus infections and granulomas. Which test confirms the likely diagnosis? DHR flow cytometry CGD (defective NADPH oxidase) is diagnosed by DHR flow cytometry. Lecture 04 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Why are patients with CGD especially prone to catalase-positive organisms? They cannot produce their own oxidative burst, and these organisms break down the small amount of H₂O₂ made The slide links defective NADPH oxidase to infections with catalase-positive organisms. The explanation that these bacteria destroy the little H₂O₂ available is a standard reasoning, not slide text. Lecture 04 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which treatment is listed for CGD? Prophylaxis, IFN-γ, stem-cell transplant CGD management: prophylaxis, IFN-γ and stem-cell transplant. Lecture 04 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which pair of cardinal signs reflects increased blood flow? Redness and heat Increased blood flow → rubor and calor. Endothelial retraction and exudate → swelling and pain. Lecture 04 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which is a typical example of CHRONIC inflammation? TB granuloma Chronic examples include TB granuloma, RA and atherosclerosis. Acute examples: cellulitis, gout flare, appendicitis. Lecture 04 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which mediator raises the hypothalamic set point in fever? PGE₂ via COX-2 IL-1, IL-6 and TNF induce COX-2 → PGE₂ in the hypothalamus. Lecture 04 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Why do antipyretics fail in heat stroke? The set point has not been reset Heat stroke does not reset the set point, so NSAIDs and paracetamol (PGE₂ blockers) do not work. Lecture 04 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which protein DECREASES during the acute-phase response? Albumin Albumin and transferrin fall; CRP, SAA, fibrinogen, haptoglobin, ferritin, hepcidin, α1-antitrypsin and complement rise. Lecture 04 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which acute-phase protein causes anaemia of inflammation by sequestering iron? Hepcidin Hepcidin sequesters iron, causing anaemia of inflammation. Lecture 04 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Long-term excess of which protein can cause AA amyloidosis? Serum amyloid A Persistently high SAA → AA amyloidosis. Lecture 04 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which sequence of peak times after a bacterial infection is correct? Procalcitonin → CRP → ESR Procalcitonin peaks first (about 24 h), then CRP (about 48 h), then ESR (about 5 days). Lecture 04 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: hs-CRP above 3 mg/L suggests: High cardiovascular risk hs-CRP: <1 low, 1–3 average, >3 high cardiovascular risk. Lecture 04 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which complement-related disorder is caused by C1-inhibitor deficiency? Hereditary angioedema C1-INH deficiency → hereditary angioedema; C5–C9 deficiency → recurrent Neisseria; CD55/59 loss → PNH. Lecture 04 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A patient on eculizumab needs which vaccine? Meningococcal Eculizumab blocks C5, impairing MAC formation, so patients need protection against Neisseria meningitidis. Lecture 04 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which cytokine mainly drives hepatic production of CRP? IL-6 IL-6 drives fever and acute-phase proteins such as CRP and procalcitonin. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which cytokine recruits neutrophils? CXCL8 (IL-8) CXCL8 (IL-8) is the neutrophil-recruiting chemokine. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: IL-12 activates NK cells, which then release: IFN-γ IL-12 activates NK cells → IFN-γ → macrophage activation. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which cytokines induce an antiviral state? Type I interferons (α, β) Type I IFN (α, β) induces an antiviral state and activates NK cells. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Before starting anti-TNF therapy, a patient should be screened for: Latent tuberculosis TNF blockade can reactivate latent TB. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which drug blocks IL-6 receptor signalling? Tocilizumab Tocilizumab blocks IL-6R; anakinra blocks IL-1. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which condition is an example of excessive cytokine release listed on the slide? CAR-T cytokine release syndrome Cytokine storm examples: sepsis, CAR-T cytokine release syndrome, severe COVID-19. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A neutrophil count of 0.4 × 10⁹/L is: Severe neutropenia with high infection risk Neutropenia is <1.5 × 10⁹/L; below 0.5 is severe. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Pus is mainly composed of: Dead neutrophils Neutrophils die within hours to days, forming pus. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which cells are tissue macrophages of the liver? Kupffer cells Kupffer = liver; microglia = brain; alveolar = lung; osteoclasts = bone. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Microglia are macrophages of the: Brain Microglia are the brain’s resident macrophages. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which cytokines do macrophages secrete? TNF, IL-1, IL-6 Macrophages secrete TNF, IL-1 and IL-6, and present antigen to T cells. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which cell is targeted by mepolizumab? Eosinophil (via anti-IL-5) Mepolizumab is an anti-IL-5 drug; IL-5 acts on eosinophils. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which cell kills helminths using major basic protein? Eosinophil Eosinophils have red granules with major basic protein and kill helminths. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which receptor binds IgE on mast cells? FcεRI IgE bound to FcεRI; allergen cross-linking → histamine release. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which lab test is helpful after anaphylaxis, reflecting mast-cell activation? Serum tryptase Mast-cell activation is assessed by serum tryptase. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: An NK cell kills a target that has lost MHC class I. This is called: Missing self recognition NK cells kill cells that lack MHC I (“missing self”). Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which NK-cell receptor allows ADCC? CD16 NK cells kill antibody-coated cells via CD16 (ADCC). Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which cell is the best antigen-presenting cell for starting primary T-cell responses ()? Dendritic cell dendritic cells are the key APCs for initiating primary T-cell responses and carry antigen to lymph nodes. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Approximately what fraction of effector cells die once antigen falls? About 90% The contraction phase removes about 90% of effector cells by apoptosis. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Failure of contraction because of FAS defects causes: Autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome (ALPS) FAS defects → ALPS. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Roughly how large can CD8 T-cell clones expand? 10⁴–10⁵-fold, peaking around day 7–10 The slide gives 10⁴–10⁵-fold growth, peaking about day 7–10. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: What is the approximate frequency of a given naïve clone? About 1 in 10⁵–10⁶ Rare naïve clones (about 1 in 10⁵–10⁶) meet antigen in lymph nodes or spleen. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which molecules transmit the signal from the BCR into the cell? Igα/Igβ (CD79a/b) The Ig tail is too short, so Igα/Igβ with ITAMs signal. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which statement about the BCR is correct? It sees native antigen without MHC; each B cell has one specificity B cells recognise native antigen directly; every BCR on one B cell binds the same epitope; CD21 binds C3d. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: CD21 on B cells binds which molecule? Complement fragment C3d CD21 binds C3d on antigen, lowering the activation threshold. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which virus uses CD21 to enter B cells? Epstein–Barr virus (EBV) EBV uses CD21 (CR2) to infect B cells. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A drug that targets CD79b for B-cell lymphoma is: Polatuzumab Anti-CD79b polatuzumab and CD19 CAR-T treat B-cell lymphoma. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: The unique shape of the antigen-binding pocket of an antibody is its: Idiotype The idiotype is the unique binding-site shape. Isotype is the heavy-chain class. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which part of an immunoglobulin binds complement and Fc receptors? Constant region The constant (C-terminal) domain mediates complement binding and Fc receptor binding. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which enzyme complex joins V, D and J gene segments? Recombinase (RAG) V(D)J recombination uses recombinase. RAG defects cause SCID. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: In the heavy chain, which segments join first? D and J D–J joining happens first, then V joins. Light chains have no D segment. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which enzyme adds random nucleotides at V, D and J junctions? TdT Terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase adds N-nucleotides without a template. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Allelic exclusion ensures that: Each lymphocyte expresses one receptor specificity Only one allele is expressed; if the first rearrangement is non-functional, the second allele is tried. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Where does positive selection of T cells occur? Thymic cortex Positive selection occurs in the cortex; negative selection in the medulla. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: T cells with high affinity for self antigen in the thymic medulla undergo: Apoptosis Negative selection removes strongly self-reactive T cells by apoptosis. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which cells express MHC class II? APCs (macrophages, dendritic cells, B cells) MHC II is on APCs only; MHC I is on all nucleated cells. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: MHC class I molecules present peptides to: CD8⁺ T cells MHC I → CD8⁺; MHC II → CD4⁺. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which are primary lymphoid organs? Bone marrow and thymus Primary: bone marrow and thymus. Secondary: spleen, lymph nodes, MALT. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: In a lymph node, T cells mainly reside in the: Paracortex B cells live in follicles; T cells in the paracortex. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A small molecule like penicillin triggers an immune response only after binding to a protein. It is a: Hapten Haptens cannot induce a response alone but can when coupled to a carrier protein. Lecture 05 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A cell cannot transport cytosolic peptides into its endoplasmic reticulum. What presentation step is most directly affected? Loading of peptides onto class I TAP transports cytosolic peptides into the endoplasmic reticulum for class I loading. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which molecule helps exchange CLIP for an antigen peptide? HLA-DM HLA-DM catalyzes peptide exchange in the class II compartment. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: An inhibitor prevents endosomal acidification in a macrophage. Which step is most directly impaired? Processing of ingested proteins for class II Acidic compartments support proteolysis and class II peptide loading. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A dendritic cell displays a peptide from a phagocytosed tumour cell on class I. What is this called? Cross-presentation Extracellular antigen can enter the class I pathway through cross-presentation. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which recognition event can occur without classical peptide–MHC presentation? A BCR binds an intact capsular polysaccharide The BCR binds intact antigen; the conventional T-cell examples use peptide–MHC. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which interaction provides classical costimulation to a naïve T cell? CD28 with B7 CD28–B7 supplies signal 2. Adhesion and coreceptor binding play different roles. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A naïve T cell recognizes peptide–MHC without adequate costimulation. What can follow? Functional anergy Recognition alone can induce unresponsiveness rather than productive activation. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which factor directly supports expansion of a newly activated T-cell clone? IL-2 Activated T cells produce IL-2 and upregulate its receptor to expand. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Why can a bacterial superantigen activate many unrelated T-cell clones? It bridges MHC II and particular TCR variable beta regions Superantigens activate clones sharing a Vβ family without normal peptide specificity. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which helper response best supports macrophage control of intracellular mycobacteria? Th1-derived IFN-γ IFN-γ from Th1 cells activates macrophages; IL-12 helps establish the response. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which pairing best describes a helminth-directed response? Th2, IL-5 and eosinophils Th2 cytokines support IgE and eosinophils, with IL-5 particularly important for eosinophils. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Recurrent mucocutaneous candidiasis suggests impairment of which pathway? Th17–IL-17 IL-17 supports barrier defence and neutrophil recruitment against Candida. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A male infant has severe enteropathy, dermatitis and early diabetes. Which regulator is most likely defective? FOXP3 FOXP3 dysfunction impairs regulatory T cells in IPEX syndrome. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: What peptide does a polysaccharide-specific B cell present after taking up a conjugate vaccine? A peptide from the carrier protein The B cell binds sugar, internalizes the linked carrier, and presents carrier peptide to helper T cells. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which pattern best fits a typical response to a plain bacterial polysaccharide? Early IgM with limited durable memory A T-independent response is typically fast and IgM-biased, with limited durable memory. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Where do germinal-centre B cells compete for intact antigen held by follicular dendritic cells? Light zone The dark zone supports proliferation and mutation; selection takes place in the light zone. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which feature changes directly during immunoglobulin class-switch recombination? The heavy-chain constant region Switching changes effector class while retaining the rearranged binding region. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which enzyme participates in both somatic hypermutation and class switching? AID Activation-induced cytidine deaminase initiates both DNA modification processes. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A boy has impaired class switching despite B-cell antigen recognition. Which missing T-cell signal best explains X-linked hyper-IgM syndrome? CD40L binding CD40 CD40L deficiency prevents effective CD40-dependent help for switching. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: What is an alternative to perforin and granzyme-mediated cytotoxicity? FasL binding Fas on the target Fas engagement triggers death-receptor-mediated apoptosis. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Why can perforin deficiency cause severe systemic inflammation? Defective killing permits prolonged immune activation Ineffective cytotoxicity can allow excessive ongoing immune activation in familial HLH. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which change best fits T-cell exhaustion during chronic antigen exposure? Reduced killing and proliferation with sustained inhibitory signalling Persistent stimulation can lead to progressive dysfunction and increased inhibitory receptor expression. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which memory T-cell population uses CCR7 to home to lymph nodes? Central memory Central memory cells recirculate through lymphoid organs and proliferate strongly on recall. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: What maintains circulating antibody titres between exposures? Long-lived plasma cells Plasma cells continue to secrete antibodies; memory B cells reactivate on re-exposure. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: What does immune imprinting explain when a virus changes its surface antigens? Recall may favour epitopes shared with the first strain Existing memory can bias the response toward shared targets from the original exposure. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which intervention gives passive protection without inducing the infant’s own antigen-specific memory? An administered RSV-neutralizing antibody An administered antibody supplies immediate protection without active priming of the recipient. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A 14-month-old has recurrent bacterial respiratory infections, absent tonsils and very few B cells. Which defect fits? Bruton tyrosine kinase deficiency BTK deficiency blocks B-cell maturation; maternal IgG temporarily masks the defect. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A newborn has a conotruncal defect, hypocalcaemia and a low T-cell count. What is the most likely explanation? Thymic and parathyroid hypoplasia The constellation points to the DiGeorge phenotype of 22q11.2 deletion. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which structure stabilizes the class I heavy chain at the surface? Beta-2 microglobulin Class I consists of a heavy chain associated with beta-2 microglobulin. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: An HLA-B27 association with ankylosing spondylitis establishes which conclusion? The allele is a risk marker, not diagnostic by itself An association changes probability without establishing causation or a diagnosis. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which population helps explain weak responses to plain polysaccharides after splenectomy? Splenic marginal-zone B cells Marginal-zone B cells provide a fast response to blood-borne polysaccharides. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which cytokines help maintain many memory T-cell populations without persistent antigen? IL-7 and IL-15 IL-7 and IL-15 support homeostasis of many memory T cells. Lecture 06 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which statement correctly distinguishes primary from secondary lymphoid organs? Primary organs are sites of lymphocyte development before antigen exposure; secondary organs are sites of antigen exposure Bone marrow and thymus generate and mature lymphocytes antigen-independently. Nodes, spleen and MALT are where antigen is encountered and responses start. Lecture 07 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which organ replaces the avian bursa of Fabricius as the site of B-cell maturation in humans? Bone marrow Humans have no bursa; the bone marrow serves that role. The 'B' name comes from the bursa experiments in chickens. Lecture 07 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which sequence of lymph flow is correct? Interstitial fluid → initial lymphatics → collecting vessels → lymph nodes → trunks → ducts → subclavian veins Lymph passes through at least one node (a compulsory checkpoint) before returning to blood via the thoracic or right lymphatic duct into the subclavian veins. Lecture 07 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A patient develops milky pleural fluid after chest surgery. Which structure was most likely injured? Thoracic duct Thoracic duct injury leaks chyle into the pleural cavity (chylothorax). Chyle is the fat-rich lymph absorbed by lacteals. Lecture 07 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which feature prevents interstitial fluid from leaking back out of initial lymphatic capillaries? Overlapping endothelial flaps acting as one-way valves, held by anchoring filaments Initial lymphatics are blind-ended; the overlapping endothelial flaps open as interstitial pressure rises and close when pressure inside is higher. Lecture 07 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which site contains red (haematopoietic) marrow in adults? Sternum and pelvis Adult red marrow is in the sternum, ribs, vertebrae, pelvis, skull and proximal femora/humeri. Long-bone shafts contain fatty yellow marrow. Lecture 07 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which pair of factors from bone marrow stromal niches supports lymphocyte development? CXCL12 (chemokine) and IL-7 (cytokine) Stromal niches supply CXCL12, IL-7 and cell contact. CCL21/CCR7 and L-selectin relate to node homing. Lecture 07 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: What is the main significance of long-lived plasma cells residing in the bone marrow? They maintain antibody levels for years after infection or vaccination Survival niche signals allow these antibody-secreting cells to live for years. Memory B cells are a separate population, and long-lived plasma cells secrete class-switched antibody (mainly IgG). Lecture 07 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: In which thymic region are Hassall's corpuscles found? Medulla Cortex = densely packed immature thymocytes; medulla = fewer, more mature cells and Hassall's corpuscles. Lecture 07 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which pairing of thymic pathology and association is correct? Thymoma — myasthenia gravis Thymoma is associated with myasthenia gravis (anti-AChR antibodies); thymic hypoplasia occurs in the 22q11.2 deletion. Lecture 07 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: T-cell receptor excision circles (TRECs) are measured to estimate what? Recent thymic output of new T cells, used in newborn screening for SCID TRECs quantify new T cells; low values in newborn screening suggest severe combined immunodeficiency. Lecture 07 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which combination directs naive lymphocytes to peripheral lymph nodes? L-selectin (CD62L) + CCR7 Node = L-selectin + CCR7; gut = α4β7 + CCR9; skin = CLA + CCR4. Lecture 07 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A patient with inflammatory bowel disease is treated with vedolizumab. Which molecule does it block, explaining its gut selectivity? Integrin α4β7 α4β7 mediates lymphocyte homing to the gut and gut-associated lymphoid tissue. Lecture 07 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Through which structure do naive lymphocytes leave the blood to enter a lymph node? High endothelial venules in the paracortex Route: blood → HEV → node → efferent lymph → thoracic duct → blood. Afferent vessels bring lymph (and antigen), not blood lymphocytes. Lecture 07 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which lymph node region contains B-cell follicles and germinal centres? Cortex Cortex = B cells = follicles (primary resting, secondary with germinal centres). Lecture 07 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A mouse lacking T cells would be expected to show depletion of which lymph node region? Paracortex The paracortex holds T cells, dendritic cells and HEVs. Follicles are the B-cell region and the medullary cords contain plasma cells. Lecture 07 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: During an active immune response, a regional lymph node is most likely to be: Tender, mobile, usually under 2 cm, and settling over weeks This is the typical reactive node. Hard, fixed, painless or growing nodes are red flags. Lecture 07 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Why does an effector T cell leave the node and enter the infected tissue? Activation switches its homing receptors so it follows the signals of the infected tissue Effector cells change address: activation alters adhesion molecules and chemokine receptors for tissue-specific homing. Lecture 07 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: How do small antigens (<70 kDa) reach the T-cell zone of a lymph node? Directly through conduits Small antigens use conduits to the T zone; large antigens are captured at the sinus. Lecture 07 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Where is a bone marrow biopsy usually taken in adults? Posterior iliac crest Posterior iliac crest is the standard site; the biopsy helps diagnose some leukaemias and lymphomas. Lecture 07 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A 25-year-old has a tender, enlarged right axillary node after a hand abrasion. What is the most appropriate initial approach? Search the drainage territory for infection, injury or tumour Localised lymphadenopathy points to its drainage area. A tender, mobile node after a wound is reassuring. Lecture 08 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which of the following is a cause of generalised lymphadenopathy? Infectious mononucleosis (EBV) Generalised causes: EBV, CMV, toxoplasmosis, HIV, TB, lymphoma, SLE, drug reactions. Lecture 08 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which node finding is a red flag? Hard, fixed, painless supraclavicular node Red flags: >2 cm or growing, hard/fixed/painless, supraclavicular (Virchow), fever/night sweats/weight loss, no infective cause. Lecture 08 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Why is excisional biopsy preferred over fine-needle aspiration when lymphoma is suspected? It preserves node architecture needed for diagnosis Diagnosing lymphoma depends on how cells are arranged and related, which requires intact architecture. Lecture 08 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which description of the spleen is correct? Largest secondary lymphoid organ, about 150 g, left upper quadrant, under ribs 9–11 The spleen is the largest secondary lymphoid organ, in the left upper quadrant under ribs 9–11; it is normally impalpable. Lecture 08 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: How does antigen reach the spleen? Through the bloodstream, since it has no afferent lymphatics The spleen filters blood; it lacks afferent lymphatics. Lecture 08 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Why are aged red cells removed in the splenic red pulp? They become less deformable and cannot pass the narrow passages, where macrophages remove them RBCs live about 120 days; later they are trapped by red-pulp macrophages. Iron from haemoglobin is recycled. Lecture 08 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which statement best describes 'pitting' by the spleen? Removal of inclusions from red cells without destroying the cell The spleen removes inclusions (e.g. nuclear remnants) from otherwise healthy RBCs. When pitting fails, Howell–Jolly bodies appear. Lecture 08 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which is NOT a function of the spleen? Draining interstitial fluid through afferent lymphatics The spleen has no afferent lymphatics; it filters blood. Lecture 08 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: The periarteriolar lymphoid sheath (PALS) is composed mainly of: T cells with dendritic cells PALS = T-cell zone of the white pulp, with dendritic cells (APCs). Follicles are the B-cell zone. Lecture 08 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which cells respond to blood-borne polysaccharide antigens without T-cell help? Marginal-zone B cells The marginal zone is the interface with blood; its B cells and macrophages capture polysaccharide antigens. Lecture 08 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Why do children under 2 years respond poorly to plain polysaccharide vaccines, and why are conjugate vaccines used? Marginal-zone responses are immature at this age Marginal-zone responses are immature under 2 years; conjugate vaccines recruit T-cell help. Lecture 08 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which blood film findings suggest absent or poorly functioning spleen? Howell–Jolly bodies, target cells and thrombocytosis Nuclear remnants are no longer pitted out; target cells and thrombocytosis are also seen. Lecture 08 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which organism is the most common cause of overwhelming post-splenectomy infection? Streptococcus pneumoniae Pneumococcus is the most common, followed by Hib and meningococcus; Capnocytophaga after dog bites. Lecture 08 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which regimen is appropriate for a patient with asplenia? Pneumococcal, Hib, MenACWY, MenB and annual influenza vaccination, with an alert card and emergency antibiotics Prevention: vaccination, antibiotic prophylaxis (especially children and first 2 years), alert card, emergency antibiotic supply, urgent review if febrile, malaria advice. Lecture 08 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: MALT lymphoid follicles resemble those of a lymph node but lack which features? A capsule and afferent lymphatics MALT is organised like a node (follicles with germinal centres, adjacent T zones) but has no capsule and no afferent lymphatics. Lecture 08 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which cells sample luminal antigen in MALT and deliver it to dendritic cells? M (microfold) cells M cells are specialised epithelial cells overlying Peyer's patches. Lecture 08 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: What is the role of the secretory component (derived from pIgR)? Remains attached to IgA and protects it from digestion in mucus The J chain joins the dimer; the secretory component protects against enzymatic digestion. Function: immune exclusion without inflammation. Lecture 08 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A patient with coeliac disease has negative IgA-based serology. Which test is most helpful next? Total serum IgA Selective IgA deficiency (~1 in 300–700) can cause false-negative coeliac serology; blood product reactions are also a risk. Lecture 08 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which cell carries antigen from the epidermis to the draining lymph node? Langerhans cell Langerhans cells are epidermal dendritic cells; resident memory T cells stay in the skin. Lecture 08 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which statement about lymphatic disease is correct? Filariasis is the most common cause of secondary lymphoedema worldwide Secondary lymphoedema: surgery, radiotherapy, tumour and filariasis (commonest worldwide). Milroy disease is primary (congenital). Lecture 08 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A patient with melanoma undergoes sentinel node biopsy. What is the sentinel node? The first node draining the tumour Mapped with dye or tracer and examined. Standard in melanoma and breast cancer; node status drives staging. Lecture 08 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Meningeal lymphatic vessels drain fluid and immune cells from the brain to which nodes? Deep cervical nodes Vessels alongside the dural sinuses carry fluid and immune cells to deep cervical nodes; studied in Alzheimer's disease and brain tumours. Lecture 08 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which feature is the biggest source of diversity in receptor repertoire generation? Junctional diversity from TdT TdT trims and adds nucleotides without a template at each join, so it is the biggest source of variety. Allelic exclusion limits each cell to one specificity; it does not create diversity. Lecture 09 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A boy has recurrent bacterial infections, almost no B cells and very low immunoglobulins, with normal T-cell numbers. Which gene is most likely defective, and at which step is B-cell development blocked? BTK, at the pre-B step X-linked agammaglobulinaemia (BTK) blocks the pre-B step. RAG1 defects would also remove T cells (SCID), and IL-2Rγ causes X-linked SCID. Lecture 09 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: An immature B cell strongly binds a multivalent self antigen in the bone marrow. What happens first? Receptor editing via re-expressed RAG and a new light chain Strong multivalent binding triggers receptor editing first (κ → λ). Deletion happens only if editing fails; anergy is the response to weak, soluble antigen. Lecture 09 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which statement about thymic selection is correct? About 90% of thymocytes die by neglect About 90% die by neglect (no binding). Weak binding gives positive selection, intermediate gives thymic Tregs, and strong binding gives negative selection. Lecture 09 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: At which stage of T-cell development does the pre-TCR checkpoint occur? Double negative, when TCR β pairs with pre-Tα In the double-negative (CD4⁻CD8⁻) stage the rearranged β chain pairs with the surrogate pre-Tα. The checkpoint confirms the β chain works; failure → apoptosis. Lecture 09 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A patient has autoimmune endocrine disease with hypoparathyroidism and chronic candidiasis, caused by failure to display tissue-specific antigens in the thymus. Which gene is mutated? AIRE AIRE loss causes APECED (APS-1): medullary epithelium no longer displays insulin, thyroglobulin and other tissue proteins, so autoreactive T cells escape. Lecture 09 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which peripheral tolerance mechanism is correctly paired with its example? Suppression: CTLA-4 on Tregs strips B7 from dendritic cells Tregs use CTLA-4, IL-2 consumption, IL-10 and TGF-β. Ignorance refers to immune-privileged sites; deletion occurs via Fas–FasL or BIM; anergy is signal 1 without signal 2. Lecture 09 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A patient develops autoimmunity because of CTLA-4 haploinsufficiency. Which drug is used for treatment? Abatacept Abatacept (CTLA-4-Ig) blocks B7 and replaces the missing CTLA-4 brake. Ibrutinib inhibits BTK; teplizumab is anti-CD3. Lecture 09 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: In the three-signal model, which pairing is correct? Signal 3: cytokines from the dendritic cell that polarise the response Signal 1 is TCR–peptide–MHC (CD4/CD8 stabilise it); signal 2 is B7 (CD80/CD86) binding CD28; signal 3 is the instructive cytokines. Lecture 09 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A naive T cell receives signal 1 without signal 2. What is the expected outcome? Anergy Signal 1 alone leads to anergy, a built-in safety mechanism. An anergic T cell shows NFAT activity only and makes no IL-2. Lecture 09 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Why do adjuvants enhance the response to a purified antigen? They supply the danger signal that raises B7 and CD40 on dendritic cells A purified antigen lacks PAMPs. Adjuvants supply danger through pattern recognition (e.g. Toll-like receptors), raising B7 and CD40 so the dendritic cell delivers signal 2. Lecture 09 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which pairing of a disease with its checkpoint failure is correct? FOXP3 loss: failure of tolerance (checkpoints 2–3), causing autoimmunity RAG and BTK defects are checkpoint 1 (working receptor) failures. FOXP3 (IPEX) and AIRE (APECED) cause autoimmunity through failed tolerance. Lecture 09 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which statement is a clinical lesson about co-stimulation? TGN1412, a CD28 superagonist, caused a cytokine storm in a first-in-human trial TGN1412 caused a cytokine storm in 2006. Teplizumab is anti-CD3 (type 1 diabetes); 22q11.2 deletion causes thymic hypoplasia; thymic output falls after puberty. Lecture 09 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which molecules cut and rejoin V, D and J gene segments? RAG1/RAG2 RAG1/RAG2 cut and rejoin the segments. TdT then trims and adds nucleotides at the junctions. Lecture 09 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: What is the correct order of antigen-receptor gene rearrangement in a developing B cell, and what does allelic exclusion ensure? Heavy chain first, then light chain; one specificity per cell Heavy-chain rearrangement (pro-B) precedes light-chain rearrangement (immature B stage). Allelic exclusion gives one specificity per cell. Lecture 09 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: What composes the pre-BCR, and which kinase transmits its signal? μ heavy chain with surrogate light chain; BTK Pre-B cells express a pre-BCR of μ chain plus surrogate light chain, signalling through Bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK). Lecture 09 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Ibrutinib is used to treat chronic lymphocytic leukaemia. What does it inhibit? BTK BTK inhibitors such as ibrutinib treat CLL. BTK mutation, in contrast, causes X-linked agammaglobulinaemia. Lecture 09 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which cells express AIRE, and what do they display to developing T cells? Medullary thymic epithelial cells; insulin, thyroglobulin and other tissue proteins AIRE in mTECs switches on tissue-restricted proteins such as insulin and thyroglobulin so autoreactive thymocytes can be deleted. Lecture 09 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A thymocyte binds self-peptide bound to MHC class I with weak affinity. What is its fate? Positive selection to a CD8⁺ single-positive cell Weak binding gives positive selection. CD8 binds MHC class I and CD4 binds MHC class II, so MHC I restriction yields a CD8⁺ cell. Lecture 09 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: An infant has hypocalcaemia and a very small thymus due to a 22q11.2 deletion. Which term describes the syndrome, and what is the treatment if there is complete athymia? DiGeorge syndrome; thymus tissue implantation 22q11.2 deletion causes thymic hypoplasia (DiGeorge syndrome); complete athymia is treated with thymus tissue implantation. Lecture 09 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which fate and gene pair correctly describes thymocytes of intermediate affinity for self-peptide–MHC? Thymic Treg; FOXP3 Intermediate affinity leads to FOXP3⁺ thymic Tregs. Loss of FOXP3 causes IPEX. Lecture 09 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: After a penetrating injury to one eye, a patient develops inflammation in the other eye. Which tolerance mechanism has failed? Ignorance of immune-privileged antigens Eye antigens are normally hidden (ignorance). Injury exposes them, and autoreactive lymphocytes attack: sympathetic ophthalmia. Lecture 09 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which therapy blocks signal 2 of T-cell activation? Abatacept Signal 2 is B7–CD28; abatacept and belatacept block it. Teplizumab (anti-CD3) targets signal 1; anti-cytokines and JAK inhibitors target signal 3. Lecture 09 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which statement correctly describes the two-way communication between T cell and dendritic cell? CD40L on activated T cells licenses the dendritic cell to make IL-12 CD40L on the activated T cell engages CD40 on the dendritic cell, licensing IL-12 production, which feeds back to shape the response. Lecture 09 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: An immature B cell encounters a weak, soluble self antigen in the bone marrow. What is the expected state of the cell? Anergic, with low surface IgM and short life Weak soluble antigen causes anergy (functional unresponsiveness): low surface IgM, short life, no response. Strong multivalent antigen triggers editing or deletion. Lecture 09 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A lymph-node biopsy shows a single dominant lymphocyte clone with an identical receptor rearrangement. Which principle supports this test, and what does the pattern indicate? Each clone has a unique V(D)J rearrangement; monoclonal pattern suggests lymphoma Because each clone carries a unique rearrangement, a monoclonal peak signals a malignant clone (lymphoma); a polyclonal pattern is a reactive process. Lecture 09 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which pair correctly matches tolerance type to the organs where it mainly occurs? Central tolerance: bone marrow and thymus; peripheral tolerance: lymph nodes and spleen Central tolerance takes place in primary lymphoid organs during development; peripheral tolerance operates in secondary lymphoid organs and tissues after maturation. Lecture 09 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which cytokines on the three-signal diagram polarise the response (signal 3)? IL-12, IL-4, IL-6 and TGF-β The diagram lists IL-12, IL-4, IL-6 and TGF-β as instructive cytokines that steer Th1, Th2, Th17 and Treg differentiation. Lecture 09 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which kinase, carried by CD4 or CD8, phosphorylates TCR ITAMs? Lck Lck is brought to the engaged receptor by CD4/CD8. Lyn is the B-cell equivalent. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A T cell receives TCR signalling without costimulation. Result? NFAT alone is activated → anergy All three arms are needed; NFAT alone gives anergy. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: SCID with normal-looking CD4 counts and failed signalling after ITAM phosphorylation: ZAP-70 deficiency ZAP-70 docks on phosphorylated ITAMs. γc loss causes X-SCID with absent T cells. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: In the T-cell DAG arm, which enzyme leads to NF-κB activation? PKCθ DAG → PKCθ → NF-κB. In B cells the isoform is PKCβ. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Tacrolimus and ciclosporin suppress T cells by: Blocking calcineurin so NFAT cannot induce IL-2 Calcineurin dephosphorylates NFAT; blocking it prevents IL-2 production. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which sequence correctly describes BCR signalling? Lyn → Syk → BLNK → BTK and PLCγ2 Lyn phosphorylates Igα/Igβ ITAMs, Syk docks, BLNK scaffolds BTK and PLCγ2. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: The CD19/CD21 co-receptor enhances B-cell activation by: Lowering the threshold via PI3K It is an amplifier acting through PI3K. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: BTK inhibitors are used to treat: CLL BTK loss causes XLA; inhibitors (ibrutinib) treat CLL. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: The high-affinity IL-2 receptor consists of: CD25 (α) + CD122 (β) + CD132 (γc) Three subunits: α, β and common γ. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: How do CD25-high Tregs restrain responses via IL-2? Act as a high-affinity IL-2 sink They compete for IL-2. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which drug blocks mTOR on the IL-2 axis? Sirolimus Basiliximab = anti-CD25; tacrolimus/ciclosporin = calcineurin. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Order of surface markers after lymphocyte activation: CD69 → CD25 → CD71 → HLA-DR CD69 hours, CD25 1–2 d, CD71 while dividing, HLA-DR 3–5 d. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Metabolic shift in activated lymphocytes and fate of ~90% of effectors: Oxidative phosphorylation → aerobic glycolysis; die by AICD Visible on PET; survivors become memory cells. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Why does rituximab (anti-CD20) often preserve serum IgG? Plasma cells have lost CD20 Plasma cells lose surface Ig and CD20 and gain CD138. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which transcription change drives plasma-cell differentiation? PAX5/BCL6 off; BLIMP-1/XBP1 on B-cell identity off, secretory machinery on. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Superantigens differ from conventional antigens because they: Bind MHC II and TCR Vβ outside the groove, activating up to 20% of T cells Conventional antigen activates ~1 in 10⁴–10⁶ T cells. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: In the TSS case, why is clindamycin added? It inhibits bacterial toxin synthesis TSS is toxin-mediated, hence negative blood cultures. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which mitogen stimulates B cells? LPS PHA and ConA stimulate T cells; pokeweed both; TSST-1 is a superantigen. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which statement is correct? Every immunogen is an antigen An antigen can be bound; an immunogen also provokes a response. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Why are proteins the best immunogens? They yield peptides for T cells Only proteins give peptides for presentation to T cells. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which is NOT an antigen factor listed on the slide? Route of administration Route is a host/administration factor. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A very low antigen dose usually: Is ignored Too little is ignored; too much can tolerise. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Most immunogenic routes: Intradermal and subcutaneous Many dendritic cells in skin; oral often favours tolerance. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Why are adjuvanted vaccines and extra doses given to older adults? Elderly respond less well Neonates and elderly respond less well. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Two siblings receive the same vaccine; one fails to respond. Best genetic explanation? Different HLA types present different peptides HLA type decides which peptides can be presented. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A malnourished patient on immunosuppressants responds poorly to a vaccine. Factor? General health Malnutrition and immunosuppressive drugs reduce responses. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Very high antigen dose can lead to: Tolerance Dose matters in both directions. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Antigens usually need a size of at least: 10 kDa Size is usually >10 kDa. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Oral antigen exposure usually favours: Tolerance (or mucosal IgA) Per slide figure. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which statement is INCORRECT? Very high doses always maximise immunity High doses can tolerise. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Standard route for most vaccines: Intramuscular Intradermal/subcutaneous are strongest; intramuscular is standard. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: The four headings in the slide figure are: Age, genes, health, the antigen Other factors that decide whether a response happens. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: An elderly patient has chronic infection and cancer and a weak vaccine response. Factors involved: Age and general health Age plus malignancy/chronic infection reduce responses. Lecture 10 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: α-Gal sugar on pig tissue, removed by gene editing for kidney transplants, is which type of antigen? Xenoantigen It comes from another species. Alloantigens differ within the same species. Lecture 11 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which test is based on heterophile antibodies? Monospot test in EBV infection Heterophile antigens cross-react across unrelated species. Lecture 11 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Superantigens differ from conventional antigens because they: Bypass the peptide groove and activate many T cells at once They link TCR and MHC outside the groove, activating a large fraction of T cells. Lecture 11 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which statement correctly contrasts B- and T-cell recognition? Antibodies bind conformational shapes; T cells see linear peptides on MHC BCRs/antibodies bind native 3D shapes; TCRs see peptide + MHC. Lecture 11 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Immune response to one epitope widens to others as tissue damage continues. This is: Epitope spreading Typical of autoimmune disease. Lecture 11 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which pair is a molecular-mimicry association? Campylobacter and Guillain-Barré Rheumatic fever follows streptococcal infection; Guillain-Barré follows Campylobacter. Lecture 11 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A virus mutates its immunodominant epitope. The result is most likely: Immune escape Most of the response targeted that epitope, so mutation lets the virus evade it. Lecture 11 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A hapten elicits a primary response only when: It is bound to a carrier protein A hapten is too small to be immunogenic alone. Lecture 11 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A drug sits in the HLA groove and changes the peptides displayed. This is the: Altered repertoire mechanism p-i is direct receptor binding; pro-hapten needs a metabolite. Lecture 11 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Poison ivy dermatitis appearing 24–72 h after exposure is: Type IV (T-cell mediated) Urushiol is a hapten binding skin proteins; delayed T-cell reaction. Lecture 11 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Why are purified protein antigens poorly immunogenic alone? They lack an innate danger signal to activate dendritic cells Adjuvants supply the innate signal (PRR activation, depot effect). Lecture 11 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which statement about adjuvants is correct? Reactogenicity reflects innate activation AS01 (MPL + QS-21) is the shingles/malaria adjuvant; LNPs also act as adjuvants; CpG 1018 acts on TLR9. Lecture 11 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which genes lie in the MHC class III region? C4, C2, factor B and TNF Class III encodes complement and TNF, not presenting molecules; β2m is on chromosome 15. Lecture 11 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Probability that two siblings from the same parents share both HLA haplotypes? 25% Four equally likely combinations; 0.5 × 0.5 = 25%. Lecture 11 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A 7-month-old has low CD4⁺ T cells, no vaccine response, oral candidiasis and HLA-DR absent on B cells. The defect is: CIITA/RFX class II transcription factor defect Bare lymphocyte syndrome II: no class II → poor CD4 selection → no T-cell help. Lecture 11 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which step trims peptides to the proper length in the class I pathway? ERAP ERAP trims peptides in the ER; TAP transports them. Lecture 11 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: How is the class II groove protected and loaded? Invariant chain blocks groove, leaving CLIP, which HLA-DM exchanges for peptide This occurs in acidified endosomes; acidification is essential. Lecture 11 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: cDC1 cells prime naive CD8⁺ T cells against exogenous antigen by: Cross-presentation on MHC class I Cross-presentation is essential for tumour and viral vaccines; cDC2 prime CD4⁺ cells. Lecture 11 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which is a consequence of MHC restriction? Engineered T-cell therapies work only with the matching HLA type T cells need peptide + self-MHC; 1–10% of T cells are alloreactive. Lecture 11 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which statement about CD1 and MR1 is correct? CD1d presents glycolipids to iNKT cells; MR1 presents vitamin B2 metabolites to MAIT cells Both are non-polymorphic and act with innate-like speed. Lecture 11 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: Which pairing is INCORRECT? Donor anti-HLA antibodies cause platelet refractoriness Patient anti-HLA antibodies cause platelet refractoriness; donor anti-HLA antibodies cause TRALI. Lecture 11 · Immunology midterm

cards.subject: Immunology
cards.search: A tumour loses β2-microglobulin. What follows? Failure of class I presentation to CD8⁺ T cells; NK cells may kill (missing self) Without β2m, class I is not displayed. Lecture 11 · Immunology midterm

vn-final-anatomy-01-02-1.text: Vertebrae and ribs develop from the {{c1::sclerotome}}.

vn-final-anatomy-01-02-2.text: The nucleus pulposus is a remnant of the {{c1::notochord}}.

vn-final-anatomy-01-02-3.text: The annulus fibrosus develops from the {{c1::sclerotome}}.

vn-final-anatomy-01-02-4.text: The epaxial muscles are supplied by the {{c1::dorsal primary rami}}.

vn-final-anatomy-01-02-5.text: The hypaxial muscles are supplied by the {{c1::ventral primary rami}}.

vn-final-anatomy-01-02-6.text: The primary ossification center of a long bone forms in the {{c1::diaphysis}}.

vn-final-anatomy-01-02-7.text: Secondary ossification centers of long bones form in the {{c1::epiphyses}}.

vn-final-anatomy-01-02-8.text: The lateral plate mesoderm supplies the limb bones and cartilage; limb muscle precursors come from the {{c1::myotome}}.

vn-final-anatomy-01-02-9.text: The upper limb rotates laterally during development; the lower limb rotates {{c1::medially}}.

vn-final-anatomy-01-02-10.text: Premature closure of the sagittal suture causes {{c1::scaphocephaly}}.

vn-final-anatomy-03-04-1.text: The superior gluteal nerve supplies gluteus medius, gluteus minimus and {{c1::tensor fasciae latae}}.

vn-final-anatomy-03-04-2.text: Gluteus maximus is supplied by the {{c1::inferior gluteal nerve}}.

vn-final-anatomy-03-04-3.text: On a Trendelenburg test, the pelvis drops on the side {{c1::opposite the affected stance leg}}.

vn-final-anatomy-03-04-4.text: Piriformis divides the greater sciatic foramen into spaces above and below it; the superior gluteal nerve exits {{c1::above piriformis}}.

vn-final-anatomy-03-04-5.text: The main nerve of the medial thigh compartment is the {{c1::obturator nerve}}.

vn-final-anatomy-03-04-6.text: The anterior cruciate ligament limits anterior translation of the {{c1::tibia relative to the femur}}.

vn-final-anatomy-03-04-7.text: The posterior cruciate ligament limits posterior translation of the {{c1::tibia relative to the femur}}.

vn-final-anatomy-03-04-8.text: The medial meniscus is attached to the {{c1::tibial collateral ligament}}.

vn-final-anatomy-03-04-9.text: The muscle that unlocks the extended knee is the {{c1::popliteus}}.

vn-final-anatomy-03-04-10.text: The patellar ligament attaches to the {{c1::tibial tuberosity}}.

vn-final-anatomy-05-06-1.text: The lumbar plexus forms mainly from the anterior rami of {{c1::L1–L4}}.

vn-final-anatomy-05-06-2.text: The femoral nerve emerges from the lateral border of {{c1::psoas major}}.

vn-final-anatomy-05-06-3.text: The obturator nerve emerges from the medial border of {{c1::psoas major}}.

vn-final-anatomy-05-06-4.text: The femoral and obturator nerves both receive fibers from {{c1::L2–L4}}.

vn-final-anatomy-05-06-5.text: The saphenous nerve is a sensory branch of the {{c1::femoral nerve}}.

vn-final-anatomy-05-06-6.text: From lateral to medial, the major structures in the femoral triangle are {{c1::nerve, artery, vein and femoral canal}}.

vn-final-anatomy-05-06-7.text: The major structure outside the femoral sheath is the {{c1::femoral nerve}}.

vn-final-anatomy-05-06-8.text: The medial compartment of the femoral sheath is the {{c1::femoral canal}}.

vn-final-anatomy-05-06-9.text: The femoral artery becomes the popliteal artery after passing through the {{c1::adductor hiatus}}.

vn-final-anatomy-05-06-10.text: The deepest major neurovascular structure in the popliteal fossa is the {{c1::popliteal artery}}.

vn-final-microbiology-01-1.text: Koplik spots in a child with cough, coryza and conjunctivitis point to {{c1::measles}}.

vn-final-microbiology-01-2.text: Cataracts, deafness and congenital heart defects are characteristic of {{c1::congenital rubella syndrome}}.

vn-final-microbiology-01-3.text: Parvovirus B19 can cause transient aplastic crisis because it infects {{c1::erythroid precursors}}.

vn-final-microbiology-01-4.text: In roseola, the rash typically appears after the {{c1::fever subsides}}.

vn-final-microbiology-01-5.text: Chickenpox can show macules, papules, vesicles and crusts {{c1::at the same time}}.

vn-final-microbiology-01-6.text: A common long-term complication of shingles is {{c1::postherpetic neuralgia}}.

vn-final-microbiology-01-7.text: Human papillomavirus types 6 and 11 commonly cause {{c1::anogenital warts}}.

vn-final-microbiology-01-8.text: Human papillomavirus types 16 and 18 are associated with {{c1::cervical cancer}}.

vn-final-microbiology-01-9.text: Molluscum contagiosum typically causes dome-shaped papules with {{c1::central umbilication}}.

vn-final-microbiology-01-10.text: Hand, foot and mouth disease can be caused by Coxsackie A viruses of the genus {{c1::Enterovirus}}.

vn-final-pharmacology-01-1.text: A first-line option for predominantly comedonal acne is a topical {{c1::retinoid}}.

vn-final-pharmacology-01-2.text: Benzoyl peroxide kills Cutibacterium acnes by releasing {{c1::free oxygen radicals}}.

vn-final-pharmacology-01-3.text: Topical clindamycin is paired with benzoyl peroxide to limit {{c1::antibiotic resistance}}.

vn-final-pharmacology-01-4.text: Common local adverse effects of topical retinoids include {{c1::dryness, peeling and irritation}}.

vn-final-pharmacology-01-5.text: An acne agent that can also reduce hyperpigmentation is {{c1::azelaic acid}}.

vn-final-pharmacology-01-6.text: Oral isotretinoin is used for severe nodulocystic acne and is strongly {{c1::teratogenic}}.

vn-final-pharmacology-01-7.text: Two laboratory abnormalities associated with isotretinoin are {{c1::raised liver enzymes and triglycerides}}.

vn-final-pharmacology-01-8.text: Estrogen in combined oral contraceptives lowers free testosterone in part by increasing {{c1::sex hormone-binding globulin}}.

vn-final-pharmacology-01-9.text: Spironolactone helps hormonal acne in part by blocking {{c1::androgen receptors}}.

vn-final-pharmacology-01-10.text: An example of topical therapy for papulopustular rosacea is {{c1::metronidazole}}.

vn-final-physiology-01-1.text: The sensory fibre class in the direct muscle stretch reflex is {{c1::group Ia}}.

vn-final-physiology-01-2.text: A Golgi tendon organ measures muscle tension and signals via {{c1::group Ib fibres}}.

vn-final-physiology-01-3.text: When the right foot withdraws from pain, the left leg supports weight by activating its {{c1::extensors}}.

vn-final-physiology-01-4.text: A visible spontaneous twitch of a motor unit is a {{c1::fasciculation}}.

vn-final-physiology-01-5.text: Spontaneous activity of one denervated muscle fibre on electromyography is a {{c1::fibrillation}}.

vn-final-physiology-01-6.text: The defining movement in an extensor plantar response is extension of the {{c1::great toe}}.

vn-final-physiology-01-7.text: Spasticity is an increase in resistance that depends on stretch {{c1::velocity}}.

vn-final-physiology-01-8.text: The gamma-aminobutyric acid receptor subtype activated by baclofen is {{c1::GABA type B}}.

vn-final-physiology-01-9.text: Presynaptic GABA type B signalling reduces transmitter release in part by reducing entry of {{c1::calcium}}.

vn-final-physiology-01-10.text: A centrally generated pattern recorded without actual stepping is called {{c1::fictive locomotion}}.

vn-final-physiology-01-11.text: Late-stance hip extension can help initiate the next phase of gait, called {{c1::swing}}.

vn-final-physiology-01-12.text: Locomotor feedback has three main roles: retiming, correcting and {{c1::reinforcing motor output}}.

vn-final-physiology-01-13.text: The part of the Rybak–McCrea model that decides when a cycle occurs is {{c1::rhythm generation}}.

vn-final-physiology-01-14.text: Contact with an obstacle can trigger a preorganized spinal response called the {{c1::stumbling corrective reaction}}.

vn-imm-mid-06-1.text: The transporter that carries cytosolic antigen peptides into the endoplasmic reticulum is {{c1::TAP}}.

vn-imm-mid-06-2.text: The usual co-receptor for T-cell recognition of peptide–MHC class I is {{c1::CD8}}.

vn-imm-mid-06-3.text: The protein associated with the MHC class I heavy chain is {{c1::beta-2 microglobulin}}.

vn-imm-mid-06-4.text: The peptide left in the MHC class II groove after invariant-chain degradation is {{c1::CLIP}}.

vn-imm-mid-06-5.text: The molecule that promotes CLIP exchange for antigen peptide is {{c1::HLA-DM}}.

vn-imm-mid-06-6.text: The classical costimulatory receptor on a naïve T cell that binds B7 is {{c1::CD28}}.

vn-imm-mid-06-7.text: The inhibitory receptor that competes with CD28 for B7 is {{c1::CTLA-4}}.

vn-imm-mid-06-8.text: The cytokine that drives expansion of a newly activated T-cell clone is {{c1::interleukin-2}}.

vn-imm-mid-06-9.text: A superantigen cross-links MHC class II to the T-cell receptor’s {{c1::variable beta region}}.

vn-imm-mid-06-10.text: Th1 cells activate macrophages primarily through {{c1::interferon gamma}}.

vn-imm-mid-06-11.text: The Th2 cytokine especially important for eosinophils is {{c1::interleukin-5}}.

vn-imm-mid-06-12.text: The helper T-cell subset that supports defence against mucocutaneous Candida is {{c1::Th17}}.

vn-imm-mid-06-13.text: The transcription factor defective in IPEX syndrome is {{c1::FOXP3}}.

vn-imm-mid-06-14.text: The cytokine produced by follicular helper T cells that supports B-cell responses is {{c1::interleukin-21}}.

vn-imm-mid-06-15.text: A B cell responding to a conjugate vaccine presents peptides from the {{c1::carrier protein}}.

vn-imm-mid-06-16.text: The germinal-centre zone where B cells compete for antigen is the {{c1::light zone}}.

vn-imm-mid-06-17.text: The enzyme needed for both somatic hypermutation and class switching is {{c1::activation-induced cytidine deaminase}}.

vn-imm-mid-06-18.text: Immunoglobulin class switching changes the heavy-chain {{c1::constant region}}.

vn-imm-mid-06-19.text: X-linked hyper-IgM syndrome classically results from deficiency of {{c1::CD40 ligand}}.

vn-imm-mid-06-20.text: The death receptor engaged by a cytotoxic T cell as an alternative to granule release is {{c1::Fas}}.

vn-imm-mid-06-21.text: The memory T-cell subset that uses CCR7 to home to lymph nodes is {{c1::central memory T cells}}.

vn-imm-mid-06-22.text: Between antigen exposures, circulating antibody is maintained by {{c1::long-lived plasma cells}}.

vn-imm-mid-06-23.text: The protein defective in X-linked agammaglobulinaemia is {{c1::Bruton tyrosine kinase}}.

vn-imm-mid-06-24.text: Cardiac outflow defects, hypocalcaemia and thymic hypoplasia suggest {{c1::22q11.2 deletion syndrome}}.

vn-mss-final-pathology-01-01.text: A flat lesion that differs only in colour is a {{c1::macule or patch}}.
