vn-mss-final-pathology-01-02.text: The lecture uses {{c1::5 mm}} to distinguish a vesicle from a bulla.

vn-mss-final-pathology-01-03.text: A transient raised lesion due to dermal oedema is a {{c1::wheal}}.

vn-mss-final-pathology-01-04.text: Thick skin with accentuated skin markings after repeated rubbing is {{c1::lichenification}}.

vn-mss-final-pathology-01-06.text: Retained nuclei in the stratum corneum define {{c1::parakeratosis}}.

vn-mss-final-pathology-01-08.text: Premature keratinisation of individual viable epidermal cells is {{c1::dyskeratosis}}.

vn-mss-final-pathology-01-09.text: Acute eczema can form intraepidermal vesicles through severe {{c1::spongiosis}}.

vn-mss-final-pathology-01-10.text: Chronic eczema has more {{c1::acanthosis and hyperkeratosis}} and less spongiosis.

vn-mss-final-pathology-01-11.text: Allergic contact dermatitis is a {{c1::delayed type IV hypersensitivity}} reaction.

vn-mss-final-pathology-01-12.text: Irritant contact dermatitis results from {{c1::direct skin injury without prior sensitisation}}.

vn-mss-final-pathology-01-13.text: The atopic triad is eczema, {{c1::asthma and allergic rhinitis}}.

vn-mss-final-pathology-01-14.text: Pinpoint bleeding after lifting a psoriasis scale is the {{c1::Auspitz sign}}.

vn-mss-final-pathology-01-15.text: New lesions at sites of skin trauma are the {{c1::Koebner phenomenon}}.

vn-mss-final-pathology-01-16.text: Munro microabscesses contain neutrophils in the {{c1::stratum corneum}}.

vn-mss-final-pathology-01-17.text: Pustules of Kogoj contain neutrophils in the {{c1::spongiotic viable epidermis}}.

vn-mss-final-pathology-01-19.text: After a follicle ruptures in acne, {{c1::neutrophils}} arrive early and foreign-body granulomas may follow.

vn-mss-final-pathology-01-20.text: Erythema nodosum is the classic {{c1::septal panniculitis}}.

vn-mss-final-pathology-01-21.text: A biopsy for suspected panniculitis must include {{c1::subcutaneous fat}}.

vn-mss-final-pathology-01-22.text: Lupus panniculitis and pancreatic panniculitis typically show a {{c1::lobular}} pattern.

vn-immunology-mid-02-9f272982a40d7e0f.text: A molecule is recognised by an antibody but does not by itself trigger an immune response. Which term fits best? {{c1::Antigen that is not an immunogen}}
vn-immunology-mid-02-9f272982a40d7e0f.extra: All immunogens are antigens, but not all antigens are immunogens. Haptens are the classic example that need a carrier.

vn-immunology-mid-02-2d4e3eeae4e7af8f.text: What is an epitope? {{c1::The small part of an antigen bound by one antibody}}
vn-immunology-mid-02-2d4e3eeae4e7af8f.extra: An epitope (antigenic determinant) is the small part of an antigen bound by one antibody.

vn-immunology-mid-02-33f1f3f17dda3e33.text: Which test is an example of serology? {{c1::Measuring HBsAg or anti-HIV in serum}}
vn-immunology-mid-02-33f1f3f17dda3e33.extra: Serology is antigen–antibody testing of serum, with HBsAg and anti-HIV as the examples on the slide.

vn-immunology-mid-02-5be6b69fda6ce9de.text: Which cells produce antibodies? {{c1::Plasma cells derived from B lymphocytes}}
vn-immunology-mid-02-5be6b69fda6ce9de.extra: Antibodies are glycoproteins secreted by plasma cells, which derive from B lymphocytes.

vn-immunology-mid-02-cb7b572c87e5a7a0.text: Which line of defence consists of phagocytic cells? {{c1::Line 2}}
vn-immunology-mid-02-cb7b572c87e5a7a0.extra: Line 1 = barriers, line 2 = phagocytes (both innate), line 3 = humoral, line 4 = cell-mediated (adaptive).

vn-immunology-mid-02-d90c6e4ad60c62ab.text: Encapsulated bacteria that evade phagocytosis are best handled by which line of defence? {{c1::Line 3 – antibodies that enhance phagocytosis}}
vn-immunology-mid-02-d90c6e4ad60c62ab.extra: The slide says antibodies (humoral immunity, line 3) help overcome the capsule by enhancing phagocytosis.

vn-immunology-mid-02-9c051ca9b498fafd.text: A person gets a splinter. A second splinter weeks later triggers exactly the same response. This illustrates: {{c1::Innate immunity, with no memory}}
vn-immunology-mid-02-9c051ca9b498fafd.extra: The splinter story shows the innate response is the same each time, starting within minutes with inflammation within hours.

vn-immunology-mid-02-16e71a89e02539f5.text: Pattern-recognition receptors such as TLRs recognise: {{c1::PAMPs and DAMPs}}
vn-immunology-mid-02-16e71a89e02539f5.extra: Innate cells sense PAMPs on microbes and DAMPs from damaged cells through PRRs like TLRs.

vn-immunology-mid-02-cee39123fff9ee38.text: Which statement about “trained immunity” fits the slide? {{c1::Innate cells can be reprogrammed despite no classic memory}}
vn-immunology-mid-02-cee39123fff9ee38.extra: The slide notes that innate immunity is generally non-memory, although trained immunity shows innate cells can be reprogrammed.

vn-immunology-mid-02-4ad70d2981370313.text: Which feature belongs to adaptive, not innate, immunity? {{c1::Rearranged BCR/TCR giving about 10⁷–10⁹ clones}}
vn-immunology-mid-02-4ad70d2981370313.extra: Adaptive receptors are rearranged by V(D)J recombination. Innate receptors are germline-encoded.

vn-immunology-mid-02-fb04ae877ae7a64f.text: MHC class II molecules present peptide to which cell? {{c1::CD4⁺ T cells}}
vn-immunology-mid-02-fb04ae877ae7a64f.extra: MHC class I → CD8⁺ T cells; MHC class II → CD4⁺ T cells.

vn-immunology-mid-02-6eb4bd157e00fa52.text: Which is signal 2 for a naïve T cell? {{c1::Co-stimulation (B7–CD28)}}
vn-immunology-mid-02-6eb4bd157e00fa52.extra: Signal 1 = TCR–peptide–MHC, signal 2 = co-stimulation (B7–CD28), signal 3 = cytokines.

vn-immunology-mid-02-cb1608e2424e58e5.text: Which antibody isotype is first to appear in a primary response? {{c1::IgM}}
vn-immunology-mid-02-cb1608e2424e58e5.extra: IgM appears first; IgG dominates later and in the secondary response.

vn-immunology-mid-02-ad13efdd9d76a22a.extra: IgG is the main antibody and is the one that crosses the placenta.

vn-immunology-mid-02-ea1386e4fa6ae699.extra: Th1 activate macrophages; Th2 eosinophils; Th17 neutrophils; Tfh help B cells make high-affinity antibodies.

vn-immunology-mid-02-119446ca7607b791.text: Which T-cell subset helps B cells make high-affinity antibodies? {{c1::Tfh}}
vn-immunology-mid-02-119446ca7607b791.extra: Tfh (follicular helper) cells help B cells make high-affinity antibodies.

vn-immunology-mid-02-9a18b1bddff2820a.text: A child receives rabies immunoglobulin after a bite. This is: {{c1::Artificial passive immunity}}
vn-immunology-mid-02-9a18b1bddff2820a.extra: Ready-made antibodies given medically are artificial passive immunity. Passive protection is immediate but short-lived, without memory.

vn-immunology-mid-02-14cdcc84af8b8405.text: Which example is natural passive immunity? {{c1::IgA in breast milk}}
vn-immunology-mid-02-14cdcc84af8b8405.extra: Maternal IgG across the placenta and IgA in milk are natural passive immunity.

vn-immunology-mid-02-336783bb4dcb34cb.text: Which of the following is true of the secondary response compared with the primary response? {{c1::Lag of 1–3 days, mainly IgG, 10–100× greater}}
vn-immunology-mid-02-336783bb4dcb34cb.extra: Memory lymphocytes give a lag of 1–3 days with mainly higher-affinity IgG, 10–100× greater and longer-lasting.

vn-immunology-mid-02-d767f1e75ba4cef1.text: Mutation of the RAG genes would most directly lead to: {{c1::SCID}}
vn-immunology-mid-02-d767f1e75ba4cef1.extra: RAG genes drive V(D)J recombination. RAG defects → SCID.

vn-immunology-mid-02-734c90cfe2b61f19.text: A defect in FOXP3 causes which condition? {{c1::IPEX}}
vn-immunology-mid-02-734c90cfe2b61f19.extra: FOXP3 defect (regulatory T cells) → IPEX; AIRE defect → APS-1.

vn-immunology-mid-02-eca0b815e81d351a.text: Which mechanism is part of PERIPHERAL tolerance? {{c1::Anergy, deletion and suppression by Tregs}}
vn-immunology-mid-02-eca0b815e81d351a.extra: Strongly self-reactive cells are deleted centrally (thymus for T, bone marrow for B); peripheral tolerance uses anergy, deletion and Treg suppression.

vn-immunology-mid-02-ea5505b2f9d4ad43.text: Which failure of immunity is defined as “too much response to harmless antigens”? {{c1::Hypersensitivity}}
vn-immunology-mid-02-ea5505b2f9d4ad43.extra: Hypersensitivity = overreaction to harmless antigens; autoimmunity = loss of self-tolerance; immunodeficiency = absent/weak response; immunoproliferative = malignant immune cells.

vn-immunology-mid-03-d9f7e7d0d1854d5a.text: Which agent restores neutrophil numbers after chemotherapy? {{c1::G-CSF (filgrastim)}}
vn-immunology-mid-03-d9f7e7d0d1854d5a.extra: G-CSF stimulates the bone marrow to produce neutrophils.

vn-immunology-mid-03-bf0ee958dccb87e1.extra: T cells mature in the thymus; NK and B cells mature in the bone marrow.

vn-immunology-mid-03-0eda06ae424785fb.text: Which of the following is a component of innate immunity? {{c1::Complement proteins}}
vn-immunology-mid-03-0eda06ae424785fb.extra: Complement, acute-phase proteins, cytokines and antimicrobial peptides are innate soluble molecules.

vn-immunology-mid-03-9343d590a198e58d.text: What is the main role of lysozyme? {{c1::Digest peptidoglycan in bacterial cell walls}}
vn-immunology-mid-03-9343d590a198e58d.extra: Lysozyme in tears and saliva digests peptidoglycan.

vn-immunology-mid-03-ed4abe6bd80f3aab.text: Defensins and cathelicidin (LL-37) work by: {{c1::Disrupting microbial membranes}}
vn-immunology-mid-03-ed4abe6bd80f3aab.extra: They are antimicrobial peptides that disrupt microbial membranes.

vn-immunology-mid-03-120297d0e3165833.text: Which is a defence of the stomach against ingested bacteria? {{c1::Gastric acid at pH 1–3}}
vn-immunology-mid-03-120297d0e3165833.extra: Gastric acid (pH 1–3), bile, peristalsis and Paneth-cell defensins protect the gut.

vn-immunology-mid-03-44c51948c55bc5d4.text: The mucociliary escalator is impaired in: {{c1::Cystic fibrosis and smoking}}
vn-immunology-mid-03-44c51948c55bc5d4.extra: The slide lists cystic fibrosis and smoking as impairing mucociliary clearance.

vn-immunology-mid-03-cb2f6b50985c18d5.text: Which organism pair is linked to antibiotic disturbance of normal flora? {{c1::Candida overgrowth and C. difficile colitis}}
vn-immunology-mid-03-cb2f6b50985c18d5.extra: Antibiotics disturb the microbiota, allowing Candida overgrowth and C. difficile colitis.

vn-immunology-mid-03-34760547dd91ef7f.text: Microbiota therapies approved to prevent recurrent infection target which organism? {{c1::C. difficile}}
vn-immunology-mid-03-34760547dd91ef7f.extra: Rebyota and Vowst are named for preventing recurrent C. difficile.

vn-immunology-mid-03-967b039ca2ced581.text: In the burn case, which defence failed first? {{c1::The skin barrier}}
vn-immunology-mid-03-967b039ca2ced581.extra: The skin barrier was lost, with burn-induced immune suppression.

vn-immunology-mid-03-4744cf19e3f4bf67.text: Which organism grew from the burn wound and blood cultures? {{c1::Pseudomonas aeruginosa}}
vn-immunology-mid-03-4744cf19e3f4bf67.extra: The case describes Pseudomonas aeruginosa, an opportunist that forms biofilms and is often drug-resistant.

vn-immunology-mid-03-460de7fb690a623f.text: What is the priority management step in the burn sepsis case? {{c1::Cultures and antipseudomonal antibiotics within 1 hour, fluids and wound excision}}
vn-immunology-mid-03-460de7fb690a623f.extra: The slide lists cultures, antipseudomonal antibiotics within 1 h, fluids and wound excision.

vn-immunology-mid-03-e3ed2c9604dbf1a8.extra: TLR4 = LPS; TLR2 = lipoproteins; TLR5 = flagellin.

vn-immunology-mid-03-0f2b4f5fd8b21775.text: Which receptor senses viral RNA in the cytosol? {{c1::RIG-I}}
vn-immunology-mid-03-0f2b4f5fd8b21775.extra: RIG-I detects viral RNA; cGAS–STING senses DNA.

vn-immunology-mid-03-85ca4e78b8ebcd87.extra: cGAS–STING is the DNA-sensing pathway on the slide.

vn-immunology-mid-03-cd56421109aea033.text: Caspase-1 activation by NLRP3 leads to production of: {{c1::Active IL-1β}}
vn-immunology-mid-03-cd56421109aea033.extra: NLR activation → caspase-1 → active IL-1β; triggered by microbes and urate crystals (gout).

vn-immunology-mid-03-1e11d4e1c075b585.text: A patient has recurrent fevers and inflammation due to an NLRP3 gain-of-function mutation. Which treatment fits? {{c1::IL-1 blockade}}
vn-immunology-mid-03-1e11d4e1c075b585.extra: NLRP3 mutations cause CAPS, treated with IL-1 blockade.

vn-immunology-mid-03-ea19adaf4a2ab0cd.text: NF-κB activation mainly results in: {{c1::Inflammatory cytokines}}
vn-immunology-mid-03-ea19adaf4a2ab0cd.extra: NF-κB → inflammatory cytokines; IRFs → type I interferons.

vn-immunology-mid-03-05655c7b4c549855.text: Heplisav-B contains an adjuvant that stimulates which receptor? {{c1::TLR9 (CpG)}}
vn-immunology-mid-03-05655c7b4c549855.extra: The TLR9 agonist CpG is the vaccine adjuvant in Heplisav-B.

vn-immunology-mid-04-3a6ee68069878bfc.text: Which of the following is a chemoattractant for phagocytes? {{c1::C5a}}
vn-immunology-mid-04-3a6ee68069878bfc.extra: Phagocytes move up gradients of C5a, CXCL8, bacterial fMLP peptides and LTB4. C3b and IgG are opsonins.

vn-immunology-mid-04-1142abcd25d674b6.text: Which molecules are opsonins named on the slide? {{c1::C3b and IgG}}
vn-immunology-mid-04-1142abcd25d674b6.extra: Opsonins that enhance attachment include C3b and IgG (also CRP and MBL).

vn-immunology-mid-04-196b75f53eab0a29.text: What is a phagosome? {{c1::A vesicle containing the engulfed microbe}}
vn-immunology-mid-04-196b75f53eab0a29.extra: Pseudopods surround the microbe, forming a phagosome that then fuses with lysosomes.

vn-immunology-mid-04-3a1e8c11faf33672.text: A patient without a spleen is most at risk from: {{c1::Encapsulated bacteria such as S. pneumoniae}}
vn-immunology-mid-04-3a1e8c11faf33672.extra: The spleen clears opsonised encapsulated bacteria. Asplenic patients need vaccines against N. meningitidis, S. pneumoniae and H. influenzae.

vn-immunology-mid-04-b583555cf4b69ed8.text: Which of the following is an encapsulated bacterium? {{c1::Haemophilus influenzae type B}}
vn-immunology-mid-04-b583555cf4b69ed8.extra: The listed examples include S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae type B, N. meningitidis, E. coli, Salmonella, Klebsiella and group B Strep.

vn-immunology-mid-04-c0fa7b48df5b8db7.text: Which adhesion molecules mediate rolling of leukocytes on activated endothelium? {{c1::E- and P-selectins}}
vn-immunology-mid-04-c0fa7b48df5b8db7.extra: Selectins mediate rolling. LFA-1 and Mac-1 bind ICAM-1 for firm adhesion after chemokines switch integrins to high affinity.

vn-immunology-mid-04-2b81bfaed3964ea1.text: Which integrins bind ICAM-1? {{c1::LFA-1 and Mac-1}}
vn-immunology-mid-04-2b81bfaed3964ea1.extra: LFA-1 and Mac-1 bind ICAM-1 for firm adhesion.

vn-immunology-mid-04-41ac40233d02d9b9.text: After tissue injury, which cells arrive first and when? {{c1::Neutrophils at 6–24 h}}
vn-immunology-mid-04-41ac40233d02d9b9.extra: Neutrophils arrive first (6–24 h), followed by monocytes (24–48 h).

vn-immunology-mid-04-d1dbc434a7aed1bf.text: A newborn has delayed umbilical cord separation, infections without pus and high neutrophil counts. Which defect fits? {{c1::LAD-I (CD18 defect)}}
vn-immunology-mid-04-d1dbc434a7aed1bf.extra: LAD-I causes delayed cord separation, infections without pus and neutrophilia.

vn-immunology-mid-04-e6e13bafe9509432.text: Natalizumab, used for multiple sclerosis, blocks: {{c1::α4 integrin}}
vn-immunology-mid-04-e6e13bafe9509432.extra: Natalizumab is anti-α4 integrin and blocks leukocyte entry into tissue.

vn-immunology-mid-04-6a58b2dc6071696d.text: Which enzyme converts H₂O₂ to hypochlorous acid in neutrophils? {{c1::Myeloperoxidase}}
vn-immunology-mid-04-6a58b2dc6071696d.extra: NADPH oxidase makes superoxide, which gives H₂O₂; myeloperoxidase turns this into hypochlorous acid (bleach).

vn-immunology-mid-04-6a535f0bb6cd2db5.text: Which cell source of nitric oxide is described on the slide? {{c1::Activated macrophages via iNOS}}
vn-immunology-mid-04-6a535f0bb6cd2db5.extra: Inducible NO synthase in activated macrophages produces NO.

vn-immunology-mid-04-7db5993fb2ab93b0.text: Which feature describes neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs)? {{c1::DNA webs with granule proteins that trap microbes}}
vn-immunology-mid-04-7db5993fb2ab93b0.extra: NETs are DNA webs studded with granule proteins; they may also drive thrombosis and autoimmunity.

vn-immunology-mid-04-914ab2dc0645ec6d.text: A child has recurrent S. aureus and Aspergillus infections and granulomas. Which test confirms the likely diagnosis? {{c1::DHR flow cytometry}}
vn-immunology-mid-04-914ab2dc0645ec6d.extra: CGD (defective NADPH oxidase) is diagnosed by DHR flow cytometry.

vn-immunology-mid-04-9fcb2c2e4c407dba.text: Why are patients with CGD especially prone to catalase-positive organisms? {{c1::They cannot produce their own oxidative burst, and these organisms break down the small amount of H₂O₂ made}}
vn-immunology-mid-04-9fcb2c2e4c407dba.extra: The slide links defective NADPH oxidase to infections with catalase-positive organisms. The explanation that these bacteria destroy the little H₂O₂ available is a standard reasoning, not slide text.

vn-immunology-mid-04-35a074317565cacb.text: Which treatment is listed for CGD? {{c1::Prophylaxis, IFN-γ, stem-cell transplant}}
vn-immunology-mid-04-35a074317565cacb.extra: CGD management: prophylaxis, IFN-γ and stem-cell transplant.

vn-immunology-mid-04-0f8a614b9a8222b9.text: Which pair of cardinal signs reflects increased blood flow? {{c1::Redness and heat}}
vn-immunology-mid-04-0f8a614b9a8222b9.extra: Increased blood flow → rubor and calor. Endothelial retraction and exudate → swelling and pain.

vn-immunology-mid-04-6966a37e424b647e.text: Which is a typical example of CHRONIC inflammation? {{c1::TB granuloma}}
vn-immunology-mid-04-6966a37e424b647e.extra: Chronic examples include TB granuloma, RA and atherosclerosis. Acute examples: cellulitis, gout flare, appendicitis.

vn-immunology-mid-04-7ab11f763e60f8ee.text: Which mediator raises the hypothalamic set point in fever? {{c1::PGE₂ via COX-2}}
vn-immunology-mid-04-7ab11f763e60f8ee.extra: IL-1, IL-6 and TNF induce COX-2 → PGE₂ in the hypothalamus.

vn-immunology-mid-04-12d7b1368512fdd8.text: Why do antipyretics fail in heat stroke? {{c1::The set point has not been reset}}
vn-immunology-mid-04-12d7b1368512fdd8.extra: Heat stroke does not reset the set point, so NSAIDs and paracetamol (PGE₂ blockers) do not work.

vn-immunology-mid-04-36c2e9bc2288694c.text: Which protein DECREASES during the acute-phase response? {{c1::Albumin}}
vn-immunology-mid-04-36c2e9bc2288694c.extra: Albumin and transferrin fall; CRP, SAA, fibrinogen, haptoglobin, ferritin, hepcidin, α1-antitrypsin and complement rise.

vn-immunology-mid-04-d6d625d4d8b9fb8e.text: Which acute-phase protein causes anaemia of inflammation by sequestering iron? {{c1::Hepcidin}}
vn-immunology-mid-04-d6d625d4d8b9fb8e.extra: Hepcidin sequesters iron, causing anaemia of inflammation.

vn-immunology-mid-04-e9052d6db476c125.text: Long-term excess of which protein can cause AA amyloidosis? {{c1::Serum amyloid A}}

vn-immunology-mid-04-d6a3be2bc42c68a8.text: Which sequence of peak times after a bacterial infection is correct? {{c1::Procalcitonin → CRP → ESR}}
vn-immunology-mid-04-d6a3be2bc42c68a8.extra: Procalcitonin peaks first (about 24 h), then CRP (about 48 h), then ESR (about 5 days).

vn-immunology-mid-04-ca7635c633366b5b.text: hs-CRP above 3 mg/L suggests: {{c1::High cardiovascular risk}}
vn-immunology-mid-04-ca7635c633366b5b.extra: hs-CRP: <1 low, 1–3 average, >3 high cardiovascular risk.

vn-immunology-mid-04-a614a8bfd62b9c3b.text: Which complement-related disorder is caused by C1-inhibitor deficiency? {{c1::Hereditary angioedema}}
vn-immunology-mid-04-a614a8bfd62b9c3b.extra: C1-INH deficiency → hereditary angioedema; C5–C9 deficiency → recurrent Neisseria; CD55/59 loss → PNH.

vn-immunology-mid-04-c4acd36c86c51295.text: A patient on eculizumab needs which vaccine? {{c1::Meningococcal}}
vn-immunology-mid-04-c4acd36c86c51295.extra: Eculizumab blocks C5, impairing MAC formation, so patients need protection against Neisseria meningitidis.

vn-immunology-mid-05-3fb290afc130ad5c.text: Which cytokine mainly drives hepatic production of CRP? {{c1::IL-6}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-3fb290afc130ad5c.extra: IL-6 drives fever and acute-phase proteins such as CRP and procalcitonin.

vn-immunology-mid-05-ccbbd0489e4f5062.text: IL-12 activates NK cells, which then release: {{c1::IFN-γ}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-ccbbd0489e4f5062.extra: IL-12 activates NK cells → IFN-γ → macrophage activation.

vn-immunology-mid-05-61a3a6c9ff35867a.text: Which cytokines induce an antiviral state? {{c1::Type I interferons (α, β)}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-61a3a6c9ff35867a.extra: Type I IFN (α, β) induces an antiviral state and activates NK cells.

vn-immunology-mid-05-17786cec73fac3e4.text: Before starting anti-TNF therapy, a patient should be screened for: {{c1::Latent tuberculosis}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-17786cec73fac3e4.extra: TNF blockade can reactivate latent TB.

vn-immunology-mid-05-cfd9b0ae33e99f4b.text: Which drug blocks IL-6 receptor signalling? {{c1::Tocilizumab}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-cfd9b0ae33e99f4b.extra: Tocilizumab blocks IL-6R; anakinra blocks IL-1.

vn-immunology-mid-05-81ab8284c374ded9.text: Which condition is an example of excessive cytokine release listed on the slide? {{c1::CAR-T cytokine release syndrome}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-81ab8284c374ded9.extra: Cytokine storm examples: sepsis, CAR-T cytokine release syndrome, severe COVID-19.

vn-immunology-mid-05-90f44ec5193d9598.text: A neutrophil count of 0.4 × 10⁹/L is: {{c1::Severe neutropenia with high infection risk}}

vn-immunology-mid-05-f85e4657983b11a3.text: Pus is mainly composed of: {{c1::Dead neutrophils}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-f85e4657983b11a3.extra: Neutrophils die within hours to days, forming pus.

vn-immunology-mid-05-ee51e58c37a87943.text: Which cells are tissue macrophages of the liver? {{c1::Kupffer cells}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-ee51e58c37a87943.extra: Kupffer = liver; microglia = brain; alveolar = lung; osteoclasts = bone.

vn-immunology-mid-05-73d118e0a85e863c.extra: Microglia are the brain’s resident macrophages.

vn-immunology-mid-05-67718512c5af7962.text: Which cytokines do macrophages secrete? {{c1::TNF, IL-1, IL-6}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-67718512c5af7962.extra: Macrophages secrete TNF, IL-1 and IL-6, and present antigen to T cells.

vn-immunology-mid-05-9db3aee324ceaba7.text: Which cell is targeted by mepolizumab? {{c1::Eosinophil (via anti-IL-5)}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-9db3aee324ceaba7.extra: Mepolizumab is an anti-IL-5 drug; IL-5 acts on eosinophils.

vn-immunology-mid-05-6df08e6f021a75d8.text: Which cell kills helminths using major basic protein? {{c1::Eosinophil}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-6df08e6f021a75d8.extra: Eosinophils have red granules with major basic protein and kill helminths.

vn-immunology-mid-05-6cefc65e064d856a.text: Which receptor binds IgE on mast cells? {{c1::FcεRI}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-6cefc65e064d856a.extra: IgE bound to FcεRI; allergen cross-linking → histamine release.

vn-immunology-mid-05-97b1310fe250f31d.text: Which lab test is helpful after anaphylaxis, reflecting mast-cell activation? {{c1::Serum tryptase}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-97b1310fe250f31d.extra: Mast-cell activation is assessed by serum tryptase.

vn-immunology-mid-05-7da18af14de41bbe.text: An NK cell kills a target that has lost MHC class I. This is called: {{c1::Missing self recognition}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-7da18af14de41bbe.extra: NK cells kill cells that lack MHC I (“missing self”).

vn-immunology-mid-05-e4c8cc73dcb72bc6.extra: NK cells kill antibody-coated cells via CD16 (ADCC).

vn-immunology-mid-05-6e21017300662f7b.text: Which cell is the best antigen-presenting cell for starting primary T-cell responses ()? {{c1::Dendritic cell}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-6e21017300662f7b.extra: dendritic cells are the key APCs for initiating primary T-cell responses and carry antigen to lymph nodes.

vn-immunology-mid-05-b9ef2f4a9299cb5d.text: Approximately what fraction of effector cells die once antigen falls? {{c1::About 90%}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-b9ef2f4a9299cb5d.extra: The contraction phase removes about 90% of effector cells by apoptosis.

vn-immunology-mid-05-61db7c0920288e06.text: Failure of contraction because of FAS defects causes: {{c1::Autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome (ALPS)}}

vn-immunology-mid-05-5cf808abc554fbda.text: Roughly how large can CD8 T-cell clones expand? {{c1::10⁴–10⁵-fold, peaking around day 7–10}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-5cf808abc554fbda.extra: The slide gives 10⁴–10⁵-fold growth, peaking about day 7–10.

vn-immunology-mid-05-a963f78cfabada33.text: What is the approximate frequency of a given naïve clone? {{c1::About 1 in 10⁵–10⁶}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-a963f78cfabada33.extra: Rare naïve clones (about 1 in 10⁵–10⁶) meet antigen in lymph nodes or spleen.

vn-immunology-mid-05-9d9403c88c13ee17.text: Which molecules transmit the signal from the BCR into the cell? {{c1::Igα/Igβ (CD79a/b)}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-9d9403c88c13ee17.extra: The Ig tail is too short, so Igα/Igβ with ITAMs signal.

vn-immunology-mid-05-8daa5b76c9b236fa.text: Which statement about the BCR is correct? {{c1::It sees native antigen without MHC; each B cell has one specificity}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-8daa5b76c9b236fa.extra: B cells recognise native antigen directly; every BCR on one B cell binds the same epitope; CD21 binds C3d.

vn-immunology-mid-05-2cbcd4a8b8c600b1.text: CD21 on B cells binds which molecule? {{c1::Complement fragment C3d}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-2cbcd4a8b8c600b1.extra: CD21 binds C3d on antigen, lowering the activation threshold.

vn-immunology-mid-05-a617baeeaa832fa9.text: Which virus uses CD21 to enter B cells? {{c1::Epstein–Barr virus (EBV)}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-a617baeeaa832fa9.extra: EBV uses CD21 (CR2) to infect B cells.

vn-immunology-mid-05-10db1ab941239921.text: A drug that targets CD79b for B-cell lymphoma is: {{c1::Polatuzumab}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-10db1ab941239921.extra: Anti-CD79b polatuzumab and CD19 CAR-T treat B-cell lymphoma.

vn-immunology-mid-05-00f363b4f84ab9cd.text: The unique shape of the antigen-binding pocket of an antibody is its: {{c1::Idiotype}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-00f363b4f84ab9cd.extra: The idiotype is the unique binding-site shape. Isotype is the heavy-chain class.

vn-immunology-mid-05-599bf1effed1a9d7.text: Which part of an immunoglobulin binds complement and Fc receptors? {{c1::Constant region}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-599bf1effed1a9d7.extra: The constant (C-terminal) domain mediates complement binding and Fc receptor binding.

vn-immunology-mid-05-b05a3917c6123a8c.text: Which enzyme complex joins V, D and J gene segments? {{c1::Recombinase (RAG)}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-b05a3917c6123a8c.extra: V(D)J recombination uses recombinase. RAG defects cause SCID.

vn-immunology-mid-05-8ee55cb99ff9a4c4.text: In the heavy chain, which segments join first? {{c1::D and J}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-8ee55cb99ff9a4c4.extra: D–J joining happens first, then V joins. Light chains have no D segment.

vn-immunology-mid-05-6ae6a74415b7f795.text: Which enzyme adds random nucleotides at V, D and J junctions? {{c1::TdT}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-6ae6a74415b7f795.extra: Terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase adds N-nucleotides without a template.

vn-immunology-mid-05-0b8a27344d2e3bc6.text: Allelic exclusion ensures that: {{c1::Each lymphocyte expresses one receptor specificity}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-0b8a27344d2e3bc6.extra: Only one allele is expressed; if the first rearrangement is non-functional, the second allele is tried.

vn-immunology-mid-05-6f86f008eafdbda1.text: Where does positive selection of T cells occur? {{c1::Thymic cortex}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-6f86f008eafdbda1.extra: Positive selection occurs in the cortex; negative selection in the medulla.

vn-immunology-mid-05-073a8e7fa2787da3.text: T cells with high affinity for self antigen in the thymic medulla undergo: {{c1::Apoptosis}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-073a8e7fa2787da3.extra: Negative selection removes strongly self-reactive T cells by apoptosis.

vn-immunology-mid-05-e2015958cb0eb333.text: Which cells express MHC class II? {{c1::APCs (macrophages, dendritic cells, B cells)}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-e2015958cb0eb333.extra: MHC II is on APCs only; MHC I is on all nucleated cells.

vn-immunology-mid-05-54e42a07cbe58126.text: MHC class I molecules present peptides to: {{c1::CD8⁺ T cells}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-54e42a07cbe58126.extra: MHC I → CD8⁺; MHC II → CD4⁺.

vn-immunology-mid-05-a61a9070de277de1.text: Which are primary lymphoid organs? {{c1::Bone marrow and thymus}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-a61a9070de277de1.extra: Primary: bone marrow and thymus. Secondary: spleen, lymph nodes, MALT.

vn-immunology-mid-05-ee69dcba0417b25f.text: In a lymph node, T cells mainly reside in the: {{c1::Paracortex}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-ee69dcba0417b25f.extra: B cells live in follicles; T cells in the paracortex.

vn-immunology-mid-05-d8a2825daf7b77e0.text: A small molecule like penicillin triggers an immune response only after binding to a protein. It is a: {{c1::Hapten}}
vn-immunology-mid-05-d8a2825daf7b77e0.extra: Haptens cannot induce a response alone but can when coupled to a carrier protein.

vn-immunology-mid-06-206e2b31b615becf.text: A cell cannot transport cytosolic peptides into its endoplasmic reticulum. What presentation step is most directly affected? {{c1::Loading of peptides onto class I}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-206e2b31b615becf.extra: TAP transports cytosolic peptides into the endoplasmic reticulum for class I loading.

vn-immunology-mid-06-b207c592612187e8.text: Which molecule helps exchange CLIP for an antigen peptide? {{c1::HLA-DM}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-b207c592612187e8.extra: HLA-DM catalyzes peptide exchange in the class II compartment.

vn-immunology-mid-06-3a42fa6a48b4a49f.text: An inhibitor prevents endosomal acidification in a macrophage. Which step is most directly impaired? {{c1::Processing of ingested proteins for class II}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-3a42fa6a48b4a49f.extra: Acidic compartments support proteolysis and class II peptide loading.

vn-immunology-mid-06-dec20d6c5e198f79.text: A dendritic cell displays a peptide from a phagocytosed tumour cell on class I. What is this called? {{c1::Cross-presentation}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-dec20d6c5e198f79.extra: Extracellular antigen can enter the class I pathway through cross-presentation.

vn-immunology-mid-06-5a64921b565239ed.text: Which recognition event can occur without classical peptide–MHC presentation? {{c1::A BCR binds an intact capsular polysaccharide}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-5a64921b565239ed.extra: The BCR binds intact antigen; the conventional T-cell examples use peptide–MHC.

vn-immunology-mid-06-590707c21b0840ef.text: Which interaction provides classical costimulation to a naïve T cell? {{c1::CD28 with B7}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-590707c21b0840ef.extra: CD28–B7 supplies signal 2. Adhesion and coreceptor binding play different roles.

vn-immunology-mid-06-55a5ff440b06720c.text: A naïve T cell recognizes peptide–MHC without adequate costimulation. What can follow? {{c1::Functional anergy}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-55a5ff440b06720c.extra: Recognition alone can induce unresponsiveness rather than productive activation.

vn-immunology-mid-06-1d7d84b7db925c70.text: Which factor directly supports expansion of a newly activated T-cell clone? {{c1::IL-2}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-1d7d84b7db925c70.extra: Activated T cells produce IL-2 and upregulate its receptor to expand.

vn-immunology-mid-06-63ca0580d1301a38.text: Why can a bacterial superantigen activate many unrelated T-cell clones? {{c1::It bridges MHC II and particular TCR variable beta regions}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-63ca0580d1301a38.extra: Superantigens activate clones sharing a Vβ family without normal peptide specificity.

vn-immunology-mid-06-39ebc25a90ee216d.text: Which helper response best supports macrophage control of intracellular mycobacteria? {{c1::Th1-derived IFN-γ}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-39ebc25a90ee216d.extra: IFN-γ from Th1 cells activates macrophages; IL-12 helps establish the response.

vn-immunology-mid-06-2a122c61eb7e8507.text: Which pairing best describes a helminth-directed response? {{c1::Th2, IL-5 and eosinophils}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-2a122c61eb7e8507.extra: Th2 cytokines support IgE and eosinophils, with IL-5 particularly important for eosinophils.

vn-immunology-mid-06-6e9629970701f446.text: Recurrent mucocutaneous candidiasis suggests impairment of which pathway? {{c1::Th17–IL-17}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-6e9629970701f446.extra: IL-17 supports barrier defence and neutrophil recruitment against Candida.

vn-immunology-mid-06-07db5b3046e99cae.text: A male infant has severe enteropathy, dermatitis and early diabetes. Which regulator is most likely defective? {{c1::FOXP3}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-07db5b3046e99cae.extra: FOXP3 dysfunction impairs regulatory T cells in IPEX syndrome.

vn-immunology-mid-06-172ba2965c676701.text: What peptide does a polysaccharide-specific B cell present after taking up a conjugate vaccine? {{c1::A peptide from the carrier protein}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-172ba2965c676701.extra: The B cell binds sugar, internalizes the linked carrier, and presents carrier peptide to helper T cells.

vn-immunology-mid-06-33b12ede9fc7da91.text: Which pattern best fits a typical response to a plain bacterial polysaccharide? {{c1::Early IgM with limited durable memory}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-33b12ede9fc7da91.extra: A T-independent response is typically fast and IgM-biased, with limited durable memory.

vn-immunology-mid-06-05161def7ab5b120.text: Where do germinal-centre B cells compete for intact antigen held by follicular dendritic cells? {{c1::Light zone}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-05161def7ab5b120.extra: The dark zone supports proliferation and mutation; selection takes place in the light zone.

vn-immunology-mid-06-2a1c0f53af36a29a.text: Which feature changes directly during immunoglobulin class-switch recombination? {{c1::The heavy-chain constant region}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-2a1c0f53af36a29a.extra: Switching changes effector class while retaining the rearranged binding region.

vn-immunology-mid-06-08e7b1568f449bcb.text: Which enzyme participates in both somatic hypermutation and class switching? {{c1::AID}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-08e7b1568f449bcb.extra: Activation-induced cytidine deaminase initiates both DNA modification processes.

vn-immunology-mid-06-1cef0f431404ffd6.text: A boy has impaired class switching despite B-cell antigen recognition. Which missing T-cell signal best explains X-linked hyper-IgM syndrome? {{c1::CD40L binding CD40}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-1cef0f431404ffd6.extra: CD40L deficiency prevents effective CD40-dependent help for switching.

vn-immunology-mid-06-73f37ef498fb3325.text: What is an alternative to perforin and granzyme-mediated cytotoxicity? {{c1::FasL binding Fas on the target}}

vn-immunology-mid-06-d9c09badeb4ff7be.text: Why can perforin deficiency cause severe systemic inflammation? {{c1::Defective killing permits prolonged immune activation}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-d9c09badeb4ff7be.extra: Ineffective cytotoxicity can allow excessive ongoing immune activation in familial HLH.

vn-immunology-mid-06-be0fd4d6998f4eec.text: Which change best fits T-cell exhaustion during chronic antigen exposure? {{c1::Reduced killing and proliferation with sustained inhibitory signalling}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-be0fd4d6998f4eec.extra: Persistent stimulation can lead to progressive dysfunction and increased inhibitory receptor expression.

vn-immunology-mid-06-1918496c84e84aec.text: Which memory T-cell population uses CCR7 to home to lymph nodes? {{c1::Central memory}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-1918496c84e84aec.extra: Central memory cells recirculate through lymphoid organs and proliferate strongly on recall.

vn-immunology-mid-06-3aa37f9463e26ded.text: What maintains circulating antibody titres between exposures? {{c1::Long-lived plasma cells}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-3aa37f9463e26ded.extra: Plasma cells continue to secrete antibodies; memory B cells reactivate on re-exposure.

vn-immunology-mid-06-4da167aac8238e8e.text: What does immune imprinting explain when a virus changes its surface antigens? {{c1::Recall may favour epitopes shared with the first strain}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-4da167aac8238e8e.extra: Existing memory can bias the response toward shared targets from the original exposure.

vn-immunology-mid-06-67d09f94c1b7480c.text: Which intervention gives passive protection without inducing the infant’s own antigen-specific memory? {{c1::An administered RSV-neutralizing antibody}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-67d09f94c1b7480c.extra: An administered antibody supplies immediate protection without active priming of the recipient.

vn-immunology-mid-06-880f43ff78e80b96.text: A 14-month-old has recurrent bacterial respiratory infections, absent tonsils and very few B cells. Which defect fits? {{c1::Bruton tyrosine kinase deficiency}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-880f43ff78e80b96.extra: BTK deficiency blocks B-cell maturation; maternal IgG temporarily masks the defect.

vn-immunology-mid-06-c1171a5a262fcb70.text: A newborn has a conotruncal defect, hypocalcaemia and a low T-cell count. What is the most likely explanation? {{c1::Thymic and parathyroid hypoplasia}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-c1171a5a262fcb70.extra: The constellation points to the DiGeorge phenotype of 22q11.2 deletion.

vn-immunology-mid-06-c05356cf6c139e32.text: Which structure stabilizes the class I heavy chain at the surface? {{c1::Beta-2 microglobulin}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-c05356cf6c139e32.extra: Class I consists of a heavy chain associated with beta-2 microglobulin.

vn-immunology-mid-06-d71398a1e714f562.text: An HLA-B27 association with ankylosing spondylitis establishes which conclusion? {{c1::The allele is a risk marker, not diagnostic by itself}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-d71398a1e714f562.extra: An association changes probability without establishing causation or a diagnosis.

vn-immunology-mid-06-61316cb2a47dc17d.text: Which population helps explain weak responses to plain polysaccharides after splenectomy? {{c1::Splenic marginal-zone B cells}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-61316cb2a47dc17d.extra: Marginal-zone B cells provide a fast response to blood-borne polysaccharides.

vn-immunology-mid-06-6d6729d4b3a430bb.text: Which cytokines help maintain many memory T-cell populations without persistent antigen? {{c1::IL-7 and IL-15}}
vn-immunology-mid-06-6d6729d4b3a430bb.extra: IL-7 and IL-15 support homeostasis of many memory T cells.

vn-immunology-mid-07-8da08696eea9ef1b.text: Which statement correctly distinguishes primary from secondary lymphoid organs? {{c1::Primary organs are sites of lymphocyte development before antigen exposure; secondary organs are sites of antigen exposure}}
vn-immunology-mid-07-8da08696eea9ef1b.extra: Bone marrow and thymus generate and mature lymphocytes antigen-independently. Nodes, spleen and MALT are where antigen is encountered and responses start.

vn-immunology-mid-07-0ef2cd5149ce99f7.text: Which organ replaces the avian bursa of Fabricius as the site of B-cell maturation in humans? {{c1::Bone marrow}}
vn-immunology-mid-07-0ef2cd5149ce99f7.extra: Humans have no bursa; the bone marrow serves that role. The 'B' name comes from the bursa experiments in chickens.

vn-immunology-mid-07-105daa36dfe525a2.text: Which sequence of lymph flow is correct? {{c1::Interstitial fluid → initial lymphatics → collecting vessels → lymph nodes → trunks → ducts → subclavian veins}}
vn-immunology-mid-07-105daa36dfe525a2.extra: Lymph passes through at least one node (a compulsory checkpoint) before returning to blood via the thoracic or right lymphatic duct into the subclavian veins.

vn-immunology-mid-07-6186a6eb13f9bf2e.text: A patient develops milky pleural fluid after chest surgery. Which structure was most likely injured? {{c1::Thoracic duct}}
vn-immunology-mid-07-6186a6eb13f9bf2e.extra: Thoracic duct injury leaks chyle into the pleural cavity (chylothorax). Chyle is the fat-rich lymph absorbed by lacteals.

vn-immunology-mid-07-3c8fdc277a4f8918.text: Which feature prevents interstitial fluid from leaking back out of initial lymphatic capillaries? {{c1::Overlapping endothelial flaps acting as one-way valves, held by anchoring filaments}}
vn-immunology-mid-07-3c8fdc277a4f8918.extra: Initial lymphatics are blind-ended; the overlapping endothelial flaps open as interstitial pressure rises and close when pressure inside is higher.

vn-immunology-mid-07-0e1c8df06b55a5b6.text: Which site contains red (haematopoietic) marrow in adults? {{c1::Sternum and pelvis}}
vn-immunology-mid-07-0e1c8df06b55a5b6.extra: Adult red marrow is in the sternum, ribs, vertebrae, pelvis, skull and proximal femora/humeri. Long-bone shafts contain fatty yellow marrow.

vn-immunology-mid-07-01543bb0e4dccfa7.text: Which pair of factors from bone marrow stromal niches supports lymphocyte development? {{c1::CXCL12 (chemokine) and IL-7 (cytokine)}}
vn-immunology-mid-07-01543bb0e4dccfa7.extra: Stromal niches supply CXCL12, IL-7 and cell contact. CCL21/CCR7 and L-selectin relate to node homing.

vn-immunology-mid-07-fd36f3066ce33165.text: What is the main significance of long-lived plasma cells residing in the bone marrow? {{c1::They maintain antibody levels for years after infection or vaccination}}
vn-immunology-mid-07-fd36f3066ce33165.extra: Survival niche signals allow these antibody-secreting cells to live for years. Memory B cells are a separate population, and long-lived plasma cells secrete class-switched antibody (mainly IgG).

vn-immunology-mid-07-30f419171167deb0.text: In which thymic region are Hassall's corpuscles found? {{c1::Medulla}}
vn-immunology-mid-07-30f419171167deb0.extra: Cortex = densely packed immature thymocytes; medulla = fewer, more mature cells and Hassall's corpuscles.

vn-immunology-mid-07-85eac9d914574b2b.text: Which pairing of thymic pathology and association is correct? {{c1::Thymoma — myasthenia gravis}}
vn-immunology-mid-07-85eac9d914574b2b.extra: Thymoma is associated with myasthenia gravis (anti-AChR antibodies); thymic hypoplasia occurs in the 22q11.2 deletion.

vn-immunology-mid-07-1c1b104f40587820.text: T-cell receptor excision circles (TRECs) are measured to estimate what? {{c1::Recent thymic output of new T cells, used in newborn screening for SCID}}
vn-immunology-mid-07-1c1b104f40587820.extra: TRECs quantify new T cells; low values in newborn screening suggest severe combined immunodeficiency.

vn-immunology-mid-07-e7bd4ac2c8824b1a.text: Which combination directs naive lymphocytes to peripheral lymph nodes? {{c1::L-selectin (CD62L) + CCR7}}
vn-immunology-mid-07-e7bd4ac2c8824b1a.extra: Node = L-selectin + CCR7; gut = α4β7 + CCR9; skin = CLA + CCR4.

vn-immunology-mid-07-62a819d79a077797.text: A patient with inflammatory bowel disease is treated with vedolizumab. Which molecule does it block, explaining its gut selectivity? {{c1::Integrin α4β7}}
vn-immunology-mid-07-62a819d79a077797.extra: α4β7 mediates lymphocyte homing to the gut and gut-associated lymphoid tissue.

vn-immunology-mid-07-f13aa32d56fffe05.text: Through which structure do naive lymphocytes leave the blood to enter a lymph node? {{c1::High endothelial venules in the paracortex}}
vn-immunology-mid-07-f13aa32d56fffe05.extra: Route: blood → HEV → node → efferent lymph → thoracic duct → blood. Afferent vessels bring lymph (and antigen), not blood lymphocytes.

vn-immunology-mid-07-46573420e5b9b5cd.text: Which lymph node region contains B-cell follicles and germinal centres? {{c1::Cortex}}
vn-immunology-mid-07-46573420e5b9b5cd.extra: Cortex = B cells = follicles (primary resting, secondary with germinal centres).

vn-immunology-mid-07-6eedba5e4bc7ab66.text: A mouse lacking T cells would be expected to show depletion of which lymph node region? {{c1::Paracortex}}
vn-immunology-mid-07-6eedba5e4bc7ab66.extra: The paracortex holds T cells, dendritic cells and HEVs. Follicles are the B-cell region and the medullary cords contain plasma cells.

vn-immunology-mid-07-4e3de0b168446fe7.text: During an active immune response, a regional lymph node is most likely to be: {{c1::Tender, mobile, usually under 2 cm, and settling over weeks}}
vn-immunology-mid-07-4e3de0b168446fe7.extra: This is the typical reactive node. Hard, fixed, painless or growing nodes are red flags.

vn-immunology-mid-07-a41a61d45630a35b.text: Why does an effector T cell leave the node and enter the infected tissue? {{c1::Activation switches its homing receptors so it follows the signals of the infected tissue}}
vn-immunology-mid-07-a41a61d45630a35b.extra: Effector cells change address: activation alters adhesion molecules and chemokine receptors for tissue-specific homing.

vn-immunology-mid-07-d209a79260fd5a2d.text: How do small antigens (<70 kDa) reach the T-cell zone of a lymph node? {{c1::Directly through conduits}}
vn-immunology-mid-07-d209a79260fd5a2d.extra: Small antigens use conduits to the T zone; large antigens are captured at the sinus.

vn-immunology-mid-07-3e601a9050b4184d.text: Where is a bone marrow biopsy usually taken in adults? {{c1::Posterior iliac crest}}
vn-immunology-mid-07-3e601a9050b4184d.extra: Posterior iliac crest is the standard site; the biopsy helps diagnose some leukaemias and lymphomas.

vn-immunology-mid-08-f29615e8d918241f.text: A 25-year-old has a tender, enlarged right axillary node after a hand abrasion. What is the most appropriate initial approach? {{c1::Search the drainage territory for infection, injury or tumour}}
vn-immunology-mid-08-f29615e8d918241f.extra: Localised lymphadenopathy points to its drainage area. A tender, mobile node after a wound is reassuring.

vn-immunology-mid-08-34fc96382d076551.text: Which of the following is a cause of generalised lymphadenopathy? {{c1::Infectious mononucleosis (EBV)}}
vn-immunology-mid-08-34fc96382d076551.extra: Generalised causes: EBV, CMV, toxoplasmosis, HIV, TB, lymphoma, SLE, drug reactions.

vn-immunology-mid-08-ad738b47e78588ba.text: Which node finding is a red flag? {{c1::Hard, fixed, painless supraclavicular node}}
vn-immunology-mid-08-ad738b47e78588ba.extra: Red flags: >2 cm or growing, hard/fixed/painless, supraclavicular (Virchow), fever/night sweats/weight loss, no infective cause.

vn-immunology-mid-08-0e21ca413f9964ac.text: Why is excisional biopsy preferred over fine-needle aspiration when lymphoma is suspected? {{c1::It preserves node architecture needed for diagnosis}}
vn-immunology-mid-08-0e21ca413f9964ac.extra: Diagnosing lymphoma depends on how cells are arranged and related, which requires intact architecture.

vn-immunology-mid-08-5746242e0b078cb0.text: Which description of the spleen is correct? {{c1::Largest secondary lymphoid organ, about 150 g, left upper quadrant, under ribs 9–11}}
vn-immunology-mid-08-5746242e0b078cb0.extra: The spleen is the largest secondary lymphoid organ, in the left upper quadrant under ribs 9–11; it is normally impalpable.

vn-immunology-mid-08-116df33de254ba9f.text: How does antigen reach the spleen? {{c1::Through the bloodstream, since it has no afferent lymphatics}}
vn-immunology-mid-08-116df33de254ba9f.extra: The spleen filters blood; it lacks afferent lymphatics.

vn-immunology-mid-08-abb2b01a604eb0c6.text: Why are aged red cells removed in the splenic red pulp? {{c1::They become less deformable and cannot pass the narrow passages, where macrophages remove them}}
vn-immunology-mid-08-abb2b01a604eb0c6.extra: RBCs live about 120 days; later they are trapped by red-pulp macrophages. Iron from haemoglobin is recycled.

vn-immunology-mid-08-92b1873d913ce7b0.text: Which statement best describes 'pitting' by the spleen? {{c1::Removal of inclusions from red cells without destroying the cell}}
vn-immunology-mid-08-92b1873d913ce7b0.extra: The spleen removes inclusions (e.g. nuclear remnants) from otherwise healthy RBCs. When pitting fails, Howell–Jolly bodies appear.

vn-immunology-mid-08-496687935cc8ff2c.text: Which is NOT a function of the spleen? {{c1::Draining interstitial fluid through afferent lymphatics}}
vn-immunology-mid-08-496687935cc8ff2c.extra: The spleen has no afferent lymphatics; it filters blood.

vn-immunology-mid-08-9eef2dd1c6f47623.text: The periarteriolar lymphoid sheath (PALS) is composed mainly of: {{c1::T cells with dendritic cells}}
vn-immunology-mid-08-9eef2dd1c6f47623.extra: PALS = T-cell zone of the white pulp, with dendritic cells (APCs). Follicles are the B-cell zone.

vn-immunology-mid-08-a24d1c7ab796ee65.text: Which cells respond to blood-borne polysaccharide antigens without T-cell help? {{c1::Marginal-zone B cells}}
vn-immunology-mid-08-a24d1c7ab796ee65.extra: The marginal zone is the interface with blood; its B cells and macrophages capture polysaccharide antigens.

vn-immunology-mid-08-6a5f1113b1d7d7fe.text: Why do children under 2 years respond poorly to plain polysaccharide vaccines, and why are conjugate vaccines used? {{c1::Marginal-zone responses are immature at this age}}
vn-immunology-mid-08-6a5f1113b1d7d7fe.extra: Marginal-zone responses are immature under 2 years; conjugate vaccines recruit T-cell help.

vn-immunology-mid-08-423d627aa626f706.text: Which blood film findings suggest absent or poorly functioning spleen? {{c1::Howell–Jolly bodies, target cells and thrombocytosis}}
vn-immunology-mid-08-423d627aa626f706.extra: Nuclear remnants are no longer pitted out; target cells and thrombocytosis are also seen.

vn-immunology-mid-08-6725faf42f99eb37.text: Which organism is the most common cause of overwhelming post-splenectomy infection? {{c1::Streptococcus pneumoniae}}
vn-immunology-mid-08-6725faf42f99eb37.extra: Pneumococcus is the most common, followed by Hib and meningococcus; Capnocytophaga after dog bites.

vn-immunology-mid-08-0c7af738bfeef69e.text: Which regimen is appropriate for a patient with asplenia? {{c1::Pneumococcal, Hib, MenACWY, MenB and annual influenza vaccination, with an alert card and emergency antibiotics}}
vn-immunology-mid-08-0c7af738bfeef69e.extra: Prevention: vaccination, antibiotic prophylaxis (especially children and first 2 years), alert card, emergency antibiotic supply, urgent review if febrile, malaria advice.

vn-immunology-mid-08-c1c2c108fdff6c15.text: MALT lymphoid follicles resemble those of a lymph node but lack which features? {{c1::A capsule and afferent lymphatics}}
vn-immunology-mid-08-c1c2c108fdff6c15.extra: MALT is organised like a node (follicles with germinal centres, adjacent T zones) but has no capsule and no afferent lymphatics.

vn-immunology-mid-08-5d422b7a5b4a3017.text: Which cells sample luminal antigen in MALT and deliver it to dendritic cells? {{c1::M (microfold) cells}}
vn-immunology-mid-08-5d422b7a5b4a3017.extra: M cells are specialised epithelial cells overlying Peyer's patches.

vn-immunology-mid-08-6677ab049bf0c52e.text: What is the role of the secretory component (derived from pIgR)? {{c1::Remains attached to IgA and protects it from digestion in mucus}}
vn-immunology-mid-08-6677ab049bf0c52e.extra: The J chain joins the dimer; the secretory component protects against enzymatic digestion. Function: immune exclusion without inflammation.

vn-immunology-mid-08-b6abd03cff60ade6.text: A patient with coeliac disease has negative IgA-based serology. Which test is most helpful next? {{c1::Total serum IgA}}
vn-immunology-mid-08-b6abd03cff60ade6.extra: Selective IgA deficiency (~1 in 300–700) can cause false-negative coeliac serology; blood product reactions are also a risk.

vn-immunology-mid-08-1de1bd6d1998dd23.text: Which cell carries antigen from the epidermis to the draining lymph node? {{c1::Langerhans cell}}
vn-immunology-mid-08-1de1bd6d1998dd23.extra: Langerhans cells are epidermal dendritic cells; resident memory T cells stay in the skin.

vn-immunology-mid-08-63ca675159d4f56f.text: Which statement about lymphatic disease is correct? {{c1::Filariasis is the most common cause of secondary lymphoedema worldwide}}
vn-immunology-mid-08-63ca675159d4f56f.extra: Secondary lymphoedema: surgery, radiotherapy, tumour and filariasis (commonest worldwide). Milroy disease is primary (congenital).

vn-immunology-mid-08-343748b803532467.text: A patient with melanoma undergoes sentinel node biopsy. What is the sentinel node? {{c1::The first node draining the tumour}}
vn-immunology-mid-08-343748b803532467.extra: Mapped with dye or tracer and examined. Standard in melanoma and breast cancer; node status drives staging.

vn-immunology-mid-08-c141d3838f847488.text: Meningeal lymphatic vessels drain fluid and immune cells from the brain to which nodes? {{c1::Deep cervical nodes}}
vn-immunology-mid-08-c141d3838f847488.extra: Vessels alongside the dural sinuses carry fluid and immune cells to deep cervical nodes; studied in Alzheimer's disease and brain tumours.

vn-immunology-mid-09-49447f5b123b5840.text: Which feature is the biggest source of diversity in receptor repertoire generation? {{c1::Junctional diversity from TdT}}
vn-immunology-mid-09-49447f5b123b5840.extra: TdT trims and adds nucleotides without a template at each join, so it is the biggest source of variety. Allelic exclusion limits each cell to one specificity; it does not create diversity.

vn-immunology-mid-09-90a0e28b913d0aac.text: A boy has recurrent bacterial infections, almost no B cells and very low immunoglobulins, with normal T-cell numbers. Which gene is most likely defective, and at which step is B-cell development blocked? {{c1::BTK, at the pre-B step}}
vn-immunology-mid-09-90a0e28b913d0aac.extra: X-linked agammaglobulinaemia (BTK) blocks the pre-B step. RAG1 defects would also remove T cells (SCID), and IL-2Rγ causes X-linked SCID.

vn-immunology-mid-09-42a0d65ed96ccd34.text: An immature B cell strongly binds a multivalent self antigen in the bone marrow. What happens first? {{c1::Receptor editing via re-expressed RAG and a new light chain}}
vn-immunology-mid-09-42a0d65ed96ccd34.extra: Strong multivalent binding triggers receptor editing first (κ → λ). Deletion happens only if editing fails; anergy is the response to weak, soluble antigen.

vn-immunology-mid-09-74f3a3f5e1c6983e.text: Which statement about thymic selection is correct? {{c1::About 90% of thymocytes die by neglect}}
vn-immunology-mid-09-74f3a3f5e1c6983e.extra: About 90% die by neglect (no binding). Weak binding gives positive selection, intermediate gives thymic Tregs, and strong binding gives negative selection.

vn-immunology-mid-09-12fe38b2c1e9d6d8.text: At which stage of T-cell development does the pre-TCR checkpoint occur? {{c1::Double negative, when TCR β pairs with pre-Tα}}
vn-immunology-mid-09-12fe38b2c1e9d6d8.extra: In the double-negative (CD4⁻CD8⁻) stage the rearranged β chain pairs with the surrogate pre-Tα. The checkpoint confirms the β chain works; failure → apoptosis.

vn-immunology-mid-09-f976d22f308ecee4.text: A patient has autoimmune endocrine disease with hypoparathyroidism and chronic candidiasis, caused by failure to display tissue-specific antigens in the thymus. Which gene is mutated? {{c1::AIRE}}
vn-immunology-mid-09-f976d22f308ecee4.extra: AIRE loss causes APECED (APS-1): medullary epithelium no longer displays insulin, thyroglobulin and other tissue proteins, so autoreactive T cells escape.

vn-immunology-mid-09-f8612bfca7566d20.text: Which peripheral tolerance mechanism is correctly paired with its example? {{c1::Suppression: CTLA-4 on Tregs strips B7 from dendritic cells}}
vn-immunology-mid-09-f8612bfca7566d20.extra: Tregs use CTLA-4, IL-2 consumption, IL-10 and TGF-β. Ignorance refers to immune-privileged sites; deletion occurs via Fas–FasL or BIM; anergy is signal 1 without signal 2.

vn-immunology-mid-09-77429bd66e33305b.text: A patient develops autoimmunity because of CTLA-4 haploinsufficiency. Which drug is used for treatment? {{c1::Abatacept}}
vn-immunology-mid-09-77429bd66e33305b.extra: Abatacept (CTLA-4-Ig) blocks B7 and replaces the missing CTLA-4 brake. Ibrutinib inhibits BTK; teplizumab is anti-CD3.

vn-immunology-mid-09-cc1c9bac3fd720d6.text: In the three-signal model, which pairing is correct? {{c1::Signal 3: cytokines from the dendritic cell that polarise the response}}
vn-immunology-mid-09-cc1c9bac3fd720d6.extra: Signal 1 is TCR–peptide–MHC (CD4/CD8 stabilise it); signal 2 is B7 (CD80/CD86) binding CD28; signal 3 is the instructive cytokines.

vn-immunology-mid-09-8e9dbc81b10e24aa.text: A naive T cell receives signal 1 without signal 2. What is the expected outcome? {{c1::Anergy}}
vn-immunology-mid-09-8e9dbc81b10e24aa.extra: Signal 1 alone leads to anergy, a built-in safety mechanism. An anergic T cell shows NFAT activity only and makes no IL-2.

vn-immunology-mid-09-5a0ad80439d289be.text: Why do adjuvants enhance the response to a purified antigen? {{c1::They supply the danger signal that raises B7 and CD40 on dendritic cells}}
vn-immunology-mid-09-5a0ad80439d289be.extra: A purified antigen lacks PAMPs. Adjuvants supply danger through pattern recognition (e.g. Toll-like receptors), raising B7 and CD40 so the dendritic cell delivers signal 2.

vn-immunology-mid-09-5772c9155e851d60.text: Which pairing of a disease with its checkpoint failure is correct? {{c1::FOXP3 loss: failure of tolerance (checkpoints 2–3), causing autoimmunity}}
vn-immunology-mid-09-5772c9155e851d60.extra: RAG and BTK defects are checkpoint 1 (working receptor) failures. FOXP3 (IPEX) and AIRE (APECED) cause autoimmunity through failed tolerance.

vn-immunology-mid-09-9c2ecf0951d9856e.text: Which statement is a clinical lesson about co-stimulation? {{c1::TGN1412, a CD28 superagonist, caused a cytokine storm in a first-in-human trial}}
vn-immunology-mid-09-9c2ecf0951d9856e.extra: TGN1412 caused a cytokine storm in 2006. Teplizumab is anti-CD3 (type 1 diabetes); 22q11.2 deletion causes thymic hypoplasia; thymic output falls after puberty.

vn-immunology-mid-09-ee301cdb35a13cb0.text: Which molecules cut and rejoin V, D and J gene segments? {{c1::RAG1/RAG2}}
vn-immunology-mid-09-ee301cdb35a13cb0.extra: RAG1/RAG2 cut and rejoin the segments. TdT then trims and adds nucleotides at the junctions.

vn-immunology-mid-09-56e53c6507f436e6.text: What is the correct order of antigen-receptor gene rearrangement in a developing B cell, and what does allelic exclusion ensure? {{c1::Heavy chain first, then light chain; one specificity per cell}}
vn-immunology-mid-09-56e53c6507f436e6.extra: Heavy-chain rearrangement (pro-B) precedes light-chain rearrangement (immature B stage). Allelic exclusion gives one specificity per cell.

vn-immunology-mid-09-c8eae60d5cd21800.text: What composes the pre-BCR, and which kinase transmits its signal? {{c1::μ heavy chain with surrogate light chain; BTK}}
vn-immunology-mid-09-c8eae60d5cd21800.extra: Pre-B cells express a pre-BCR of μ chain plus surrogate light chain, signalling through Bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK).

vn-immunology-mid-09-8d1c1bd2000866cb.text: Ibrutinib is used to treat chronic lymphocytic leukaemia. What does it inhibit? {{c1::BTK}}
vn-immunology-mid-09-8d1c1bd2000866cb.extra: BTK inhibitors such as ibrutinib treat CLL. BTK mutation, in contrast, causes X-linked agammaglobulinaemia.

vn-immunology-mid-09-801ddc36a3685f97.text: Which cells express AIRE, and what do they display to developing T cells? {{c1::Medullary thymic epithelial cells; insulin, thyroglobulin and other tissue proteins}}
vn-immunology-mid-09-801ddc36a3685f97.extra: AIRE in mTECs switches on tissue-restricted proteins such as insulin and thyroglobulin so autoreactive thymocytes can be deleted.

vn-immunology-mid-09-df7dc194dcac60f4.text: A thymocyte binds self-peptide bound to MHC class I with weak affinity. What is its fate? {{c1::Positive selection to a CD8⁺ single-positive cell}}
vn-immunology-mid-09-df7dc194dcac60f4.extra: Weak binding gives positive selection. CD8 binds MHC class I and CD4 binds MHC class II, so MHC I restriction yields a CD8⁺ cell.

vn-immunology-mid-09-ed1af0ca1273acad.text: An infant has hypocalcaemia and a very small thymus due to a 22q11.2 deletion. Which term describes the syndrome, and what is the treatment if there is complete athymia? {{c1::DiGeorge syndrome; thymus tissue implantation}}
vn-immunology-mid-09-ed1af0ca1273acad.extra: 22q11.2 deletion causes thymic hypoplasia (DiGeorge syndrome); complete athymia is treated with thymus tissue implantation.

vn-immunology-mid-09-bac75a0709e58ef0.text: Which fate and gene pair correctly describes thymocytes of intermediate affinity for self-peptide–MHC? {{c1::Thymic Treg; FOXP3}}
vn-immunology-mid-09-bac75a0709e58ef0.extra: Intermediate affinity leads to FOXP3⁺ thymic Tregs. Loss of FOXP3 causes IPEX.

vn-immunology-mid-09-0bda9ab70106548a.text: After a penetrating injury to one eye, a patient develops inflammation in the other eye. Which tolerance mechanism has failed? {{c1::Ignorance of immune-privileged antigens}}
vn-immunology-mid-09-0bda9ab70106548a.extra: Eye antigens are normally hidden (ignorance). Injury exposes them, and autoreactive lymphocytes attack: sympathetic ophthalmia.

vn-immunology-mid-09-b587616c0867871e.text: Which therapy blocks signal 2 of T-cell activation? {{c1::Abatacept}}
vn-immunology-mid-09-b587616c0867871e.extra: Signal 2 is B7–CD28; abatacept and belatacept block it. Teplizumab (anti-CD3) targets signal 1; anti-cytokines and JAK inhibitors target signal 3.

vn-immunology-mid-09-02f775804fd3b886.text: Which statement correctly describes the two-way communication between T cell and dendritic cell? {{c1::CD40L on activated T cells licenses the dendritic cell to make IL-12}}
vn-immunology-mid-09-02f775804fd3b886.extra: CD40L on the activated T cell engages CD40 on the dendritic cell, licensing IL-12 production, which feeds back to shape the response.

vn-immunology-mid-09-7dea6370dceba677.text: An immature B cell encounters a weak, soluble self antigen in the bone marrow. What is the expected state of the cell? {{c1::Anergic, with low surface IgM and short life}}
vn-immunology-mid-09-7dea6370dceba677.extra: Weak soluble antigen causes anergy (functional unresponsiveness): low surface IgM, short life, no response. Strong multivalent antigen triggers editing or deletion.

vn-immunology-mid-09-30724492426e86c5.text: A lymph-node biopsy shows a single dominant lymphocyte clone with an identical receptor rearrangement. Which principle supports this test, and what does the pattern indicate? {{c1::Each clone has a unique V(D)J rearrangement; monoclonal pattern suggests lymphoma}}
vn-immunology-mid-09-30724492426e86c5.extra: Because each clone carries a unique rearrangement, a monoclonal peak signals a malignant clone (lymphoma); a polyclonal pattern is a reactive process.

vn-immunology-mid-09-a58609b69664af4e.text: Which pair correctly matches tolerance type to the organs where it mainly occurs? {{c1::Central tolerance: bone marrow and thymus; peripheral tolerance: lymph nodes and spleen}}
vn-immunology-mid-09-a58609b69664af4e.extra: Central tolerance takes place in primary lymphoid organs during development; peripheral tolerance operates in secondary lymphoid organs and tissues after maturation.

vn-immunology-mid-09-493f4f8ce4f7c04c.text: Which cytokines on the three-signal diagram polarise the response (signal 3)? {{c1::IL-12, IL-4, IL-6 and TGF-β}}
vn-immunology-mid-09-493f4f8ce4f7c04c.extra: The diagram lists IL-12, IL-4, IL-6 and TGF-β as instructive cytokines that steer Th1, Th2, Th17 and Treg differentiation.

vn-immunology-mid-10-787ba8ae60a798c5.text: Which kinase, carried by CD4 or CD8, phosphorylates TCR ITAMs? {{c1::Lck}}
vn-immunology-mid-10-787ba8ae60a798c5.extra: Lck is brought to the engaged receptor by CD4/CD8. Lyn is the B-cell equivalent.

vn-immunology-mid-10-8e1b517b6fa7fbb0.text: A T cell receives TCR signalling without costimulation. Result? {{c1::NFAT alone is activated → anergy}}
vn-immunology-mid-10-8e1b517b6fa7fbb0.extra: All three arms are needed; NFAT alone gives anergy.

vn-immunology-mid-10-ee0fede33ae26e0f.text: SCID with normal-looking CD4 counts and failed signalling after ITAM phosphorylation: {{c1::ZAP-70 deficiency}}
vn-immunology-mid-10-ee0fede33ae26e0f.extra: ZAP-70 docks on phosphorylated ITAMs. γc loss causes X-SCID with absent T cells.

vn-immunology-mid-10-d5de6f3f89b7fa7e.text: In the T-cell DAG arm, which enzyme leads to NF-κB activation? {{c1::PKCθ}}
vn-immunology-mid-10-d5de6f3f89b7fa7e.extra: DAG → PKCθ → NF-κB. In B cells the isoform is PKCβ.

vn-immunology-mid-10-03e5d86c2515a65e.text: Tacrolimus and ciclosporin suppress T cells by: {{c1::Blocking calcineurin so NFAT cannot induce IL-2}}
vn-immunology-mid-10-03e5d86c2515a65e.extra: Calcineurin dephosphorylates NFAT; blocking it prevents IL-2 production.

vn-immunology-mid-10-2453b6be7ea9dacc.text: Which sequence correctly describes BCR signalling? {{c1::Lyn → Syk → BLNK → BTK and PLCγ2}}
vn-immunology-mid-10-2453b6be7ea9dacc.extra: Lyn phosphorylates Igα/Igβ ITAMs, Syk docks, BLNK scaffolds BTK and PLCγ2.

vn-immunology-mid-10-bed2440d6fd67445.text: The CD19/CD21 co-receptor enhances B-cell activation by: {{c1::Lowering the threshold via PI3K}}
vn-immunology-mid-10-bed2440d6fd67445.extra: It is an amplifier acting through PI3K.

vn-immunology-mid-10-a91b921e8a1181dc.text: BTK inhibitors are used to treat: {{c1::CLL}}
vn-immunology-mid-10-a91b921e8a1181dc.extra: BTK loss causes XLA; inhibitors (ibrutinib) treat CLL.

vn-immunology-mid-10-0794b5f424859913.text: The high-affinity IL-2 receptor consists of: {{c1::CD25 (α) + CD122 (β) + CD132 (γc)}}
vn-immunology-mid-10-0794b5f424859913.extra: Three subunits: α, β and common γ.

vn-immunology-mid-10-520bf3be4f907dbb.text: How do CD25-high Tregs restrain responses via IL-2? {{c1::Act as a high-affinity IL-2 sink}}

vn-immunology-mid-10-4a638a461d191b5c.text: Which drug blocks mTOR on the IL-2 axis? {{c1::Sirolimus}}

vn-immunology-mid-10-925f8c0ed4cc3d33.text: Order of surface markers after lymphocyte activation: {{c1::CD69 → CD25 → CD71 → HLA-DR}}
vn-immunology-mid-10-925f8c0ed4cc3d33.extra: CD69 hours, CD25 1–2 d, CD71 while dividing, HLA-DR 3–5 d.

vn-immunology-mid-10-e1bd0c4056d1a33f.text: Metabolic shift in activated lymphocytes and fate of ~90% of effectors: {{c1::Oxidative phosphorylation → aerobic glycolysis; die by AICD}}
vn-immunology-mid-10-e1bd0c4056d1a33f.extra: Visible on PET; survivors become memory cells.

vn-immunology-mid-10-c19fc93b07382b10.text: Why does rituximab (anti-CD20) often preserve serum IgG? {{c1::Plasma cells have lost CD20}}
vn-immunology-mid-10-c19fc93b07382b10.extra: Plasma cells lose surface Ig and CD20 and gain CD138.

vn-immunology-mid-10-6ab1e595c9539741.text: Which transcription change drives plasma-cell differentiation? {{c1::PAX5/BCL6 off; BLIMP-1/XBP1 on}}
vn-immunology-mid-10-6ab1e595c9539741.extra: B-cell identity off, secretory machinery on.

vn-immunology-mid-10-7d0deeaef0be743f.text: Superantigens differ from conventional antigens because they: {{c1::Bind MHC II and TCR Vβ outside the groove, activating up to 20% of T cells}}
vn-immunology-mid-10-7d0deeaef0be743f.extra: Conventional antigen activates ~1 in 10⁴–10⁶ T cells.

vn-immunology-mid-10-7b377381902b1c9f.text: In the TSS case, why is clindamycin added? {{c1::It inhibits bacterial toxin synthesis}}
vn-immunology-mid-10-7b377381902b1c9f.extra: TSS is toxin-mediated, hence negative blood cultures.

vn-immunology-mid-10-f6f36dfbe22f4229.extra: PHA and ConA stimulate T cells; pokeweed both; TSST-1 is a superantigen.

vn-immunology-mid-10-aeb2ebeb312bd496.text: Which statement is correct? {{c1::Every immunogen is an antigen}}
vn-immunology-mid-10-aeb2ebeb312bd496.extra: An antigen can be bound; an immunogen also provokes a response.

vn-immunology-mid-10-c293801b16cb3d53.text: Why are proteins the best immunogens? {{c1::They yield peptides for T cells}}
vn-immunology-mid-10-c293801b16cb3d53.extra: Only proteins give peptides for presentation to T cells.

vn-immunology-mid-10-b3896a62e0c1e938.text: Which is NOT an antigen factor listed on the slide? {{c1::Route of administration}}

vn-immunology-mid-10-833acd19e85db4d9.text: A very low antigen dose usually: {{c1::Is ignored}}
vn-immunology-mid-10-833acd19e85db4d9.extra: Too little is ignored; too much can tolerise.

vn-immunology-mid-10-cba1b06d76ad8b2c.extra: Many dendritic cells in skin; oral often favours tolerance.

vn-immunology-mid-10-5bb92c05e465cc14.text: Why are adjuvanted vaccines and extra doses given to older adults? {{c1::Elderly respond less well}}
vn-immunology-mid-10-5bb92c05e465cc14.extra: Neonates and elderly respond less well.

vn-immunology-mid-10-11ebd4bfdbbf1073.text: Two siblings receive the same vaccine; one fails to respond. Best genetic explanation? {{c1::Different HLA types present different peptides}}
vn-immunology-mid-10-11ebd4bfdbbf1073.extra: HLA type decides which peptides can be presented.

vn-immunology-mid-10-167b293499d1ef2f.text: A malnourished patient on immunosuppressants responds poorly to a vaccine. Factor? {{c1::General health}}
vn-immunology-mid-10-167b293499d1ef2f.extra: Malnutrition and immunosuppressive drugs reduce responses.

vn-immunology-mid-10-9eda4e649be7f69a.text: Very high antigen dose can lead to: {{c1::Tolerance}}

vn-immunology-mid-10-6e355982a7caf314.text: Antigens usually need a size of at least: {{c1::10 kDa}}

vn-immunology-mid-10-0e2fd139dae16f65.text: Oral antigen exposure usually favours: {{c1::Tolerance (or mucosal IgA)}}

vn-immunology-mid-10-4390665b2b2ed25b.text: Which statement is INCORRECT? {{c1::Very high doses always maximise immunity}}

vn-immunology-mid-10-92997e41788521ff.extra: Intradermal/subcutaneous are strongest; intramuscular is standard.

vn-immunology-mid-10-b380366be414190c.text: The four headings in the slide figure are: {{c1::Age, genes, health, the antigen}}
vn-immunology-mid-10-b380366be414190c.extra: Other factors that decide whether a response happens.

vn-immunology-mid-10-6ddad48c47c3427e.text: An elderly patient has chronic infection and cancer and a weak vaccine response. Factors involved: {{c1::Age and general health}}
vn-immunology-mid-10-6ddad48c47c3427e.extra: Age plus malignancy/chronic infection reduce responses.

vn-immunology-mid-11-548542737b7378d2.text: α-Gal sugar on pig tissue, removed by gene editing for kidney transplants, is which type of antigen? {{c1::Xenoantigen}}
vn-immunology-mid-11-548542737b7378d2.extra: It comes from another species. Alloantigens differ within the same species.

vn-immunology-mid-11-9042b741436822fb.text: Which test is based on heterophile antibodies? {{c1::Monospot test in EBV infection}}
vn-immunology-mid-11-9042b741436822fb.extra: Heterophile antigens cross-react across unrelated species.

vn-immunology-mid-11-ef0430f093308d95.text: Superantigens differ from conventional antigens because they: {{c1::Bypass the peptide groove and activate many T cells at once}}
vn-immunology-mid-11-ef0430f093308d95.extra: They link TCR and MHC outside the groove, activating a large fraction of T cells.

vn-immunology-mid-11-bab3fa5ff814f63b.text: Which statement correctly contrasts B- and T-cell recognition? {{c1::Antibodies bind conformational shapes; T cells see linear peptides on MHC}}
vn-immunology-mid-11-bab3fa5ff814f63b.extra: BCRs/antibodies bind native 3D shapes; TCRs see peptide + MHC.

vn-immunology-mid-11-d2606e2058d85293.text: Immune response to one epitope widens to others as tissue damage continues. This is: {{c1::Epitope spreading}}

vn-immunology-mid-11-efc47e5923126470.text: Which pair is a molecular-mimicry association? {{c1::Campylobacter and Guillain-Barré}}
vn-immunology-mid-11-efc47e5923126470.extra: Rheumatic fever follows streptococcal infection; Guillain-Barré follows Campylobacter.

vn-immunology-mid-11-8be1b7f2f6eab3fa.text: A virus mutates its immunodominant epitope. The result is most likely: {{c1::Immune escape}}
vn-immunology-mid-11-8be1b7f2f6eab3fa.extra: Most of the response targeted that epitope, so mutation lets the virus evade it.

vn-immunology-mid-11-f8d38d137fab3951.text: A hapten elicits a primary response only when: {{c1::It is bound to a carrier protein}}
vn-immunology-mid-11-f8d38d137fab3951.extra: A hapten is too small to be immunogenic alone.

vn-immunology-mid-11-1d78353324c9f3d3.text: A drug sits in the HLA groove and changes the peptides displayed. This is the: {{c1::Altered repertoire mechanism}}
vn-immunology-mid-11-1d78353324c9f3d3.extra: p-i is direct receptor binding; pro-hapten needs a metabolite.

vn-immunology-mid-11-e99d5348e1cfa81f.text: Poison ivy dermatitis appearing 24–72 h after exposure is: {{c1::Type IV (T-cell mediated)}}
vn-immunology-mid-11-e99d5348e1cfa81f.extra: Urushiol is a hapten binding skin proteins; delayed T-cell reaction.

vn-immunology-mid-11-eb2ee2577847433c.text: Why are purified protein antigens poorly immunogenic alone? {{c1::They lack an innate danger signal to activate dendritic cells}}
vn-immunology-mid-11-eb2ee2577847433c.extra: Adjuvants supply the innate signal (PRR activation, depot effect).

vn-immunology-mid-11-916f7f5b5eae4bb7.text: Which statement about adjuvants is correct? {{c1::Reactogenicity reflects innate activation}}
vn-immunology-mid-11-916f7f5b5eae4bb7.extra: AS01 (MPL + QS-21) is the shingles/malaria adjuvant; LNPs also act as adjuvants; CpG 1018 acts on TLR9.

vn-immunology-mid-11-27d687359e96980b.text: Which genes lie in the MHC class III region? {{c1::C4, C2, factor B and TNF}}
vn-immunology-mid-11-27d687359e96980b.extra: Class III encodes complement and TNF, not presenting molecules; β2m is on chromosome 15.

vn-immunology-mid-11-6d6025ab1660111e.text: Probability that two siblings from the same parents share both HLA haplotypes? {{c1::25%}}

vn-immunology-mid-11-3bc86ac579ff01dd.text: A 7-month-old has low CD4⁺ T cells, no vaccine response, oral candidiasis and HLA-DR absent on B cells. The defect is: {{c1::CIITA/RFX class II transcription factor defect}}
vn-immunology-mid-11-3bc86ac579ff01dd.extra: Bare lymphocyte syndrome II: no class II → poor CD4 selection → no T-cell help.

vn-immunology-mid-11-2ff0f9b603fc1487.text: Which step trims peptides to the proper length in the class I pathway? {{c1::ERAP}}
vn-immunology-mid-11-2ff0f9b603fc1487.extra: ERAP trims peptides in the ER; TAP transports them.

vn-immunology-mid-11-3c90b2054edf08c2.text: How is the class II groove protected and loaded? {{c1::Invariant chain blocks groove, leaving CLIP, which HLA-DM exchanges for peptide}}
vn-immunology-mid-11-3c90b2054edf08c2.extra: This occurs in acidified endosomes; acidification is essential.

vn-immunology-mid-11-1ba9bd79be87e1b8.text: cDC1 cells prime naive CD8⁺ T cells against exogenous antigen by: {{c1::Cross-presentation on MHC class I}}
vn-immunology-mid-11-1ba9bd79be87e1b8.extra: Cross-presentation is essential for tumour and viral vaccines; cDC2 prime CD4⁺ cells.

vn-immunology-mid-11-448eb463c5d67e21.text: Which is a consequence of MHC restriction? {{c1::Engineered T-cell therapies work only with the matching HLA type}}
vn-immunology-mid-11-448eb463c5d67e21.extra: T cells need peptide + self-MHC; 1–10% of T cells are alloreactive.

vn-immunology-mid-11-a13bd18e777dcb26.text: Which statement about CD1 and MR1 is correct? {{c1::CD1d presents glycolipids to iNKT cells; MR1 presents vitamin B2 metabolites to MAIT cells}}
vn-immunology-mid-11-a13bd18e777dcb26.extra: Both are non-polymorphic and act with innate-like speed.

vn-immunology-mid-11-045d169e67754733.text: Which pairing is INCORRECT? {{c1::Donor anti-HLA antibodies cause platelet refractoriness}}
vn-immunology-mid-11-045d169e67754733.extra: Patient anti-HLA antibodies cause platelet refractoriness; donor anti-HLA antibodies cause TRALI.

vn-immunology-mid-11-cb7e018b3fd7ec39.text: A tumour loses β2-microglobulin. What follows? {{c1::Failure of class I presentation to CD8⁺ T cells; NK cells may kill (missing self)}}
vn-immunology-mid-11-cb7e018b3fd7ec39.extra: Without β2m, class I is not displayed.
